Nvidia has reinstated co-founder Jensen Huang as CEO less than two weeks after he stepped down, and less than a week after the firm's board remarked it had no intention of bringing him back. Reactions to Huang's return have been a mix of praise, criticism, and jokes, with several other tech executives rallying around him.

Nvidia announced Huang's resignation on Nov. 12, a day after the board accepted it with immediate effect. He stepped down amid reports that he'd had extramarital affairs with both an alleged Chinese spy and a Nvidia employee, with allegations of a third affair with another worker subsequently surfacing. His relationship with Alice Huang (no relation) drew particular scrutiny, as she was suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips. She previously led Megaspeed, a firm U.S. authorities have been investigating over concerns it smuggled advanced Nvidia chips to China in circumvention of U.S. restrictions.

According to recent reports, while Huang said that he would be "honored" to return as CEO if asked, the board stated said on Nov. 17 that it did not plan to bring him back. Yet after reported pressure from President Donald Trump, the chipmaker has put Huang back in the top job after all. In a press release announcing Huang's reinstatement, Nvidia stated that it had based the decision on "input from senior levels of the United States government.".

"The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," remarked Nvidia board chair Harvey Jones, who last week said that the company "does not intend to reinstate Jensen.".

Trump has been characteristically celebratory about Nvidia's decision, making several posts on his social media platform Truth Social on the topic. This included an edited image based on a photo of Trump after a shooter attempted to assassinate him in 2024. Originally posted by X account @grandoldmemes, the picture has been edited to show Huang holding a red bra aloft as a Nvidia banner is displayed in the background.

Calling Huang's reinstatement an "absolutely GREAT decision" (emphasis original), Trump stated that having him installed as Nvidia's CEO is vital to the U.S. economy.

It has been revealed that "The Country needs Jensen’s leadership at Nvidia in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Organization, but the American Economy," wrote Trump. "The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to Nvidia poses any risk to National Security…. On a personal note, I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure.".

The U.S. president also spoke about Huang's reinstatement in a phone call to CNBC on Monday.

According to recent reports, "I think he's gonna start off at an almost higher level," Trump stated. "He's apologised for [his] indiscretion, which was unfortunate. Probably that’s what brought it to such a level, because sex sells, fellas. Now [CNBC host Jim] Cramer would not know that because he’s a very, very, very committed person. But sex sells.".

Trump's on-and-off ally Elon Musk also celebrated Huang's return, reposting Nvidia's announcement on X and writing that "the mistake has been corrected." Last week, Musk stated that he was signing a petition to reinstate Nvidia's then-ousted CEO.

Industry observers note that "Everyone I know at Nvidia wanted Jensen back and it shows," the Tesla and SpaceX CEO continued, sharing a post from investor Gavin Baker. In it, Baker shared images of people crowding around Huang and applauding him on his return to Nvidia's offices.

It has been revealed that "Grateful to the President, everyone in the administration, everyone who signed the petition, everyone who supported Jensen publicly, everyone who called the board, everyone on the board who fought for him, everyone," Baker wrote. Various other prominent figures in tech have also voiced support for Huang's return, several of whom have previously faced comparable turmoil at their own companies.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman appeared to express approval for Huang's reinstatement, publishing a post on X that simply read, "Jensen!" Altman went through a similar incident when OpenAI's board fired him in 2023, accusing him of lying, retaliating against critics, and creating a "toxic atmosphere." Despite these allegations, Altman was ultimately reinstated after days of outcry from supporters.

Meanwhile, Binance co-founder and former CEO Changpeng Zhao posted to X that he was "glad to see @JensenHuang back," resharing his previous reaction that it was "a mistake for Nvidia to let Jensen resign." Zhao resigned from his role as CEO of Binance and pleaded guilty to failing to maintain an effective anti-money laundering program in 2023, serving a four-month prison sentence. However, he remains Binance's majority shareholder and retains significant influence over the global cryptocurrency exchange.

"Jensen is a great man, flawed like the rest of us, but at the same time the best amongst us," Kalanick posted to X on Monday. "The world and humanity needs him to fight for a shot at liberty, a counterweight to techno-authoritarianism.".

Kalanick resigned from his role as Uber CEO in 2017 after demands from multiple major investors. This came after Kalanick took a leave of absence amid allegations of a misogynistic workplace culture. Though one of the investors sued Kalanick for fraud later that year, the ousted CEO remained on Uber's board until resigning in 2019.

Industry observers note that telegram CEO Pavel Durov also celebrated Huang's return, posting "Jensen's back" with a party popper emoji. He then joked about the situation, writing that "Nvidia's board finally accepted that a CEO has to evaluate Chinese models personally. You can't delegate that.".

According to recent reports, durov was ousted from his former role as CEO of Russian social media platform VK in 2014 after the board said it had accepted a resignation he'd submitted and failed to withdraw. Durov claimed the resignation had been an April Fools' joke and suggested that his firing was politically motivated.

Given their own personal experiences, it's no surprise that many former and current tech executives have supported Huang's return as Nvidia's CEO. Other reactions have been a mixed bag — some celebrating the news, some condemning it, and others simply enjoying the jokes and memes.

According to recent reports, "Reinstating Huang is a disaster for corporate governance and even the rule of law, but it is objectively very very funny," author and tech reporter David Z. Morris posted to X.

Some have also noted the timing of Huang's temporary ousting, joking that he deliberately orchestrated several days away from work in order to play Grand Theft Auto VI.

In a recent development, it's been a tumultuous few weeks for Nvidia, and it's unclear how the organization prepares to move forward at this stage. However, whatever happens, the jokes will likely continue for a while.

Footballers may be among the fittest athletes in the world of sport, but they are not immune to bizarre injuries.

Dave Beasant famously severed a tendon in his significant toe when he dropped a bottle of salad cream, while Rio Ferdinand strained tendons in his knee by lying in one position on the sofa for too long watching television.

The latest inductee into the strange injury hall of fame is Chelmsford City captain Cav Miley.

The 31-year-old midfielder missed the 2-2 draw with Walton and Hersham in the National League South on Saturday after twisting an ankle in training by falling down a badger hole.

Miley returned for the 1-0 home victory over Maidstone United on Monday, after which manager Mark Cooper shed more light on the incident.

"Everyone is telling me it's gone viral, but I told the truth - he fell down a badger hole," Cooper told the club's YouTube channel.

"I was told at the start it was a fox hole, but then the guy at where we train told me it's a badger hole.

"We need to make sure we fill all of them in before we train now.".

Miley joined Chelmsford in the summer after spells in the National League with Southend United and Eastleigh.

Friedrich Christian "Mick" Flick, an art collector, investor and multimillionaire who belonged to one of Germany's richest business dynasties, has died aged 82 in Rosenheim in the southern state of Bavaria, his family has noted.

The family remarked in a statement issued on Saturday that Flick left behind "the memory of a life shaped by significant acts of generosity as a donor and patron, particularly in contemporary art and in promoting tolerance.".

Flick was the grandson of Friedrich Flick, who made a huge fortune in the Nazi era with his coal and steel business, partly by using forced labor.

This past came back to haunt the grandson in 2003 when he pledged to loan his world-famous collection of modern art to Berlin, with the Central Council of Jews in Germany calling the Flick Collection a "Göring Collection" and saying the loan was intended to wash clean the "blood money" from the Nazi era.

The collection, which contains some 2,500 works by 150 artists, was exhibited in parts in the German capital from 2004 to 2021.

Flick later stated in an interview that the widespread outrage, while hurtful, had forced him to look more closely at his family's history.

In a recent development, according to his family, Flick once said: "I have no guilt for my forefathers' conduct, but I feel a responsibility, a very special responsibility. Every German bears this responsibility. As a Flick, I bear it twice.".

Among other things, he collaborated with the Prussian Cultural Heritage Foundation, which oversees Berlin's museums, to research his family's Nazi past.

He also set up a foundation in Potsdam, near Berlin, that aimed to combat xenophobia and racism and contributed €5 million ($5.4 million) to the foundation to compensate former forced laborers.

The family was also involved in a highly publicized party donations scandal in the 1980s that became known as the "Flick Affair.".

Sources indicate that "Mick" Flick married Countess Maya von Schönburg (1958-2019), the older sister of well-known socialite, businesswoman, art collector and artist Gloria von Thurn und Taxis, in 1985. The couple had three children.

German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier is setting off on a five-day trip to Africa that will take him to Ivory Coast, Ghana and Kenya.

Steinmeier will be accompanied by a business delegation and is expected to focus on economic cooperation and the training of skilled workers during the trip.

On Monday, Steinmeier is to be received by Ivorian President Allassane Outtara in Abidjan, Ivory Coast's largest city and seat of government.

The next day, in the Ghanaian capital, Accra, he is set to open the German-African Business Summit, which, according to its website, "brings together senior business executives, policymakers, investors, and industry leaders from across Germany and Africa.".

On Wednesday, he will be received by Kenyan President William Ruto in Nairobi.

In Kenya, Steinmeier will also visit the Crescent Island Game Sanctuary on Thursday, the last day of his trip.

The Federal Institute for Hydrology (BfG) has said it expects water levels in large rivers in western Germany, including the Rhine, to return to average or above in the next few days amid sustained rainfall.

It said the water level at the key gauge in Kaub near Koblenz, located at an notable bottleneck on the Middle Rhine, could reach some 3.3 meters (10.8 feet), more than 3 meters higher than the last recorded low-water readings.

The BfG remarked it also expected rising water levels in the Weser and Danube rivers, with smaller increases in the Elbe and Oder.

The rising water level in the Rhine, an crucial shipping route, means that conditions for water-borne cargo transport have improved, according to Germany's inland navigation association BDB.

"The more abundant rainfall in the past days has caused the water level in the Rhine to rise considerably, and they will keep rising a great deal in the next few days as well, meaning that each ship has much more transport capacity again," mentioned Fabian Spiess, the deputy manager at BDB.

In the middle of the year, many ships were forced to drastically reduce the loads they carried, leading to economic losses that will not be recuperated any time soon, according to Spiess.

He cited the year 2018, in which shipping on the Rhine was also hindered by extremely low water levels, saying that the months of improved conditions at the end of that year had not been enough to make good the economic damage incurred.

The conservation NGO also said that the current rain provided temporary relief to the environment but could not compensate for the negative consequences of the long dry period.

It said species of animals, such as amphibians and water insects, that lived in small bodies of water and moist habitats had been particularly impacted.

Justice Minister Stefanie Hubig says that she intends to tighten the law on murders committed with "gender-specific" motives, with a particular focus on femicides perpetrated by men who are unable to accept a separation or the desire of a woman to live a self-determined life.

"A man kills, or attempts to kill, his partner or ex-partner almost every day in Germany," Hubig told the Sunday edition of the mass-circulation Bild newspaper.

According to recent reports, "Any man killing a woman because she wants to leave him must be punished as a murderer," she mentioned, noting that in some cases, courts cite a man's deep sadness or fear of losing a partner to someone else as extenuating circumstances. This can lead to a lesser conviction of manslaughter.

She noted that in future, courts should look more closely at such motives to determine whether they were based on sentiments of patriarchal possessiveness.

However, Hubig, who belongs to the center-left Social Democrats (SPD), said she was opposed to making femicide a separate category of crime, as some women's rights organizations have demanded.

She mentioned that, in her opinion, doing so would have "no advantages over what we are intending — and much bigger disadvantages.".

The proposals are currently being debated within the coalition government and are expected to be presented to the states and associations for consideration before the end of the year.

They will then have to go before the Cabinet before being put before the parliament.

The powerful IG Metall union stated on Sunday it would call another 24-hour strike on Monday as a pay dispute continues.

Altogether, some 23,000 workers at 19 companies in northern Germany have been called upon to participate, including employees at automaker Mercedes-Benz, shipbuilding company Meyer Werft and wind ​energy company Siemens Gamesa.

The union said that a strike on Friday saw some 12,300 workers walk out at 17 facilities.

It claims that the strikes are meant to increase the pressure on employers to yield to its demands, which include a 5% ‌wage increase.

So far, employers have ⁠offered a one-off payment next year and a 1.3% wage increase from July 2028.

A fresh goal celebration was devised by Borussia Dortmund midfielder Felix Nmecha after his previous one caused controversy due to its religious aspect.

After scoring the goal that secured Dortmund's 1-0 victory over Borussia Mönchengladbach (see entry below), Nmecha knelt on one knee and crossed his arms in front of his chest. He then spread his arms, appearing to pray with his eyes closed.

Nmecha told broadcaster Sky that he intends to continue expressing his faith during goal celebrations, adding that he had once again given glory to Jesus.

Industry observers note that however, he did not perform the controversial part of his usual goal celebration. In it, he removes an imaginary crown from his head and places it on the pitch in front of him while kneeling.

This celebration has been heavily criticized, even by Dortmund's fan department.

Nmecha explained that the celebrations is about "putting down my 'crown' in front of the soon-to-come king and point out to Jesus, my hope and my strength.".

The gesture is used by Ballers in God, a network of Christian football players that has been criticized for the homophobic and queerphobic statements made by its members.

Dortmund president Hans-Joachim Watzke stated he asked the player not to do the celebration again.

Borussia Dortmund midfielder Felix Nmecha led his team to the top of the German Bundesliga table with a 1-0 victory over last-place Borussia Mönchengladbach.

Meanwhile, Bayern Munich was held to a 1-1 draw at home by Cologne on Friday, and striker Harry Kane suffered a serious ankle injury. The Ballon d'Or winner is set to miss several months after undergoing ankle surgery earlier on Saturday.

Now, Dortmund has 24 points after 10 games, putting them two points ahead of Bayern and third-place Freiburg, who defeated Elversberg 1-0.

Bundesliga powerhouse Bayern Munich concluded the 2025-26 financial year with record figures.

According to the financial report released Saturday at the club's annual general meeting, the club's total turnover was €988.2 million ($1.08 billion) — that is around €10 million more than the previous year.

Industry observers note that operating profit (EBITDA) increased from €187.8 million to €190.8 million. Pre-tax profit was €35.3 million, and net profit for the year was €22.8 million.

In a recent development, bayern had a particularly strong year in terms of sponsorships. Turnover increased by nearly €30 million, reaching €268.4 million. The club also set a record in merchandise sales, earning €152.8 million.

Industry observers note that "We have achieved another record year," CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen said. "This shows that our club has a strong foundation. And we continue to invest to ensure the best possible conditions for the sporting success of our teams.".

Moreover, Bayern achieved another milestone. They reached 500,000 members — more than any other club in the world.

Over the past 12 years, the German giants have doubled their membership, growing from 250,000 in 2014 to 500,000 this year.

"Record champions, record members, record member champions," president Herbert Hainer said.

Members hold a 70% stake in the club, which is well above the simple majority required by German rules.

The remaining 30% is owned by four German companies with roots in Bavaria: Adidas, Audi, Allianz, and Viessmann.

Bayern won the league and cup double in the 2025-26 season, losing only three of 53 games across all competitions. In Europe, the club made it to the Champions League semifinals.

Two and a half weeks after his sudden death, Free Voters leader Hubert Aiwanger, who was Bavarian Minister of Economic Affairs and Deputy Minister-President, was laid to rest in his hometown of Inkofen in Lower Bavaria.

A memorial service was held at the Parish Church of the Presentation of the Lord and broadcast on a screen outside. According to the organizers, around 2,000 people attended the solemn service.

Sources indicate that aiwanger's funeral was open to the public. His longtime partner, Tanja Schweiger, the Regensburg district administrator (Free Voters), stated that Aiwanger had been "a man of the people.".

For that reason, she said, everyone "who liked and appreciated him" was warmly welcome. The politician had already been honored with a state funeral in Munich a week earlier.

Aiwanger was found dead in a Berlin hotel on November 4 after canceling an appointment for health reasons. The 55-year-old died of natural causes.

Harry Kane, Bayern Munich's star striker, has pledged to return to the field for the important matches at the end of the current campaign after undergoing surgery for a torn ankle ligament.

"I'll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season," he wrote on social media above a photo of himself on his hospital bed, also thanking fans for their messages of support.

Kane, 33, was injured around 20 minutes into Bayern's 1-1 home draw with Cologne in their Bundesliga match on Friday.

Bayern issued a statement on Saturday saying that Kane had "successfully undergone surgery" on his left ankle but was expected to be out for three to four months.

England captain Kane, who finished the 2025–26 season with over 70 goals for club and country, was awarded the Ballon d'Or for his efforts.

Brad Pitt is sitting out of this one adventure.

One week after attending the Los Angeles premiere of The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth in Los Angeles, the actor unexpectedly skipped the Netflix movie’s red carpet rollout in London due to illness.

Ahead of the Nov. 23 event, its organizers told British outlet The Independent in a statement that Pitt was “is no longer able to attend the premiere as he has come down with flu and has been advised not to travel.".

Amid his sickness, the 62-year-old made the decision to focus on the long-term health of himself and his cast.

“He has had the flu for a few days and didn’t want to get anyone sick,” a source close to Pitt told E! News. “He is recovering and looking forward to future screenings.”.

Pitt’s costars Elizabeth Debicki, Scott Caan, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II and Peter Weller, as well as director David Fincher, still attended the premiere, which was held at the BFI IMAX in the English capital.

While Pitt may not have been present at The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth’s latest premiere, the film—a sequel to Quentin Tarantino’s 2019 movie Once Upon a Time... in Hollywood—is missing his onscreen wingman Leonardo DiCaprio entirely after the Titanic alum opted to sit out.

"It would have been great fun, but it required a lot of prosthetics, which is a good couple of weeks prepping to get him," Pitt told The Hollywood Reporter earlier this month, referring to how the trailer teased that DiCaprio's Rick Dalton character had become "too fat" for his titular stuntman to serve as a body double. "It’s hardly worth the cost for a cameo.".

He added, "It was talked about for a while, but it just seemed like a substantial ask.”.

And DiCaprio confirmed he wouldn’t reprise his role ahead of the sequel, too.

Sources indicate that “There were some talks about it early on,” he told Deadline last year. Still, he added, “Ultimately, I cannot wait to see the Cliff Booth story, but I’m not in it.”.

While Pitt is returning to reprise his Oscar-winning role, read on to learn about the legendary parts he turned down.

It has been revealed that pitt was almost the One. "I did pass on 'The Matrix," the superstar recently admitted at the Santa Barbara International Film Festival in January. "I took the red pill. That's the only one I'm naming…I wasn't offered two or three. Only the first one, just to clarify that.".

As we all know, Keanu Reeves went on to be Neo, and is presently filming the fourth film in the franchise, though producer Lorenzeo di Bonaventura once revealed Will Smith, Leonardo DiCaprio and Sandra Bullock were all in consideration in addition to Pitt.

Recent findings suggest that while it's hard to imagine anyone but Billy Crudup as Russell Hammond in Cameron Crowe's 2000 classic Almost Famous, Pitt was originally set to play the complicated rocker. But, according to the writer and director, who wrote the part with the star in mind, Pitt worked with Crowe for months before ultimately leaving the project, making way for Crudup to have his breakthrough performance.

  • Nike mentioned Tuesday ahead of its first investor day in nine years that it was reaffirming its 2027 financial guidance.
  • It has been revealed that the retailer also laid out a financial framework and stated that by the end of fiscal 2031 it's targeting approximately $5 billion in incremental revenue growth from fiscal year 2027, operating margins of 12% to 14% and adjusted earnings per share of $3.00 to $3.50.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nike mentioned Tuesday ahead of its first investor day in nine years that it was reaffirming its 2027 financial guidance.

It has been revealed that the retailer also laid out a financial framework and stated that by the end of fiscal 2031 it's targeting approximately $5 billion in incremental revenue growth from fiscal year 2027, operating margins of 12% to 14% and adjusted earnings per share of $3.00 to $3.50. The company said higher-quality revenue, gross margin expansion and productivity improvements would help it reach its goals.

Nike's 2027 financial guidance includes expectations for revenue to decline in the high-single-digit range, an adjusted operating margin of approximately 6%, and adjusted EPS of $1.15 to $1.35.

The tech giant also introduced a strategy it's calling Full Stride Ahead, which the company said aims "to get closer to athletes and focus resources on the greatest opportunities for long-term growth.".

Nike CEO Elliott Hill told CNBC's Sara Eisen that the latest initiative is about "being closer to the athletes we serve.".

"What's different today is the depth and breadth we're taking from an innovation perspective," Hill stated.

In a recent development, he added that Nike is emphasizing sportswear at a time when sports have never been more relevant around the world. Hill also noted Nike is working to regain its cultural relevance, after a perceived dropoff contributed to its slowdown both in its home market and in China.

Nike said it would focus on performance sports and sportswear opportunities "with the greatest potential for long-term growth," and said its five priority sports would be running, training, global football, basketball and outdoor.

Nike is holding an investor day at its Oregon headquarters Tuesday as the tech giant aims to prove to investors that its turnaround strategy is yielding success after a yearslong slump.

Industry observers note that last month, the company reported mixed fiscal first-quarter results as it announced a restructuring plan, including layoffs that it stated would start next year. It's the company's third round of layoffs to be announced this year.

Nike's net income and revenue both fell during the most recent period compared with a year ago, and the manufacturer stated it expects revenue to decline by a high single-digit percentage in fiscal 2027.

The fresh strategy, dubbed Pace, focuses on the company's supply chain and reorganizing into three geographies. Nike noted the turnaround strategy is expected to deliver roughly $2.5 billion in savings through fiscal 2031.

According to recent reports, nike has been seeing significant sustained declines in its China market, where revenue last quarter dropped 26%. Experts have noted the company is losing relevance in the country, while Nike has said it's actively working to win over younger consumers.

At the same time, Nike unveiled last quarter that it's creating a newly introduced global campus in India as part of its new growth strategy, hoping the country will help boost its performance. The manufacturer noted it was remaining focused on China even as it begins to build out its India presence.

Nike COO Venkatesh Alagirisamy told CNBC the tech giant sees an opportunity to triple its business in the country over the next five years.

He added that Nike's broader strategy will position it for success in India.

"If you look at the three components, brand building, landing those innovations into marketplaces in an increasingly locally connected fashion and then doing all of those things in a much faster pace really aligns well with the aspirations for India," he said.

According to recent reports, CEO Elliott Hill's turnaround strategy includes improving different parts of the business at different rates based on priority. While it's seen some signs of progress in the North America business, Hill has stated that performance isn't enough to offset the pressures on the organization elsewhere, including internationally.

The Nike consumer has also been under increased macroeconomic pressure as geopolitical tensions mount and inflation rises.

Shares of Nike have fallen 50% over the past two years.

Nintendo Store — Out of stock right now, but you can add it to your wishlist to get pinged the second a restock hits.

Amazon — Dropping tiny batches of consoles randomly throughout the day.

Walmart — Stock exists but only for third-party listings selling at way over market price, so make sure your in-stock email alerts are turned on.

According to recent reports, the remake rebuilds the 1998 classic from the ground up with modernized controls, a fully orchestrated soundtrack, reworked dungeon puzzles, and expanded Hyrule environments. The package includes the special-edition Switch 2 system sporting a custom black-and-gold finish, themed Joy-Con 2 controllers, and a matching dock decorated with the gold Triforce emblem. It retains the platform's signature flexibility, letting you switch between TV, Tabletop, and Handheld modes whenever you want. In a recent development, the magnetic Joy-Con 2 controllers add mouse-style tracking in supported games, while the new GameChat hub lets you voice chat and share your screen directly as you play. It also plays your older Switch games and supports standard multiplayer options.

Landing limited-edition Nintendo hardware takes a little prep work, but these battle-tested habits will give you a real edge over the bots:.

Hands off the refresh button in Best Buy's queue — When an online drop goes live, Best Buy puts shoppers into a randomized waiting line to filter out scrapers. Touching the reload button resets your spot and boots you straight to the back.

Sources indicate that watch for Walmart+ early-access paywalls — Walmart frequently locks headline console drops behind paid Walmart+ subscriptions for the first 30 to 60 minutes. If you have a membership, keep that tab signed in; if not, wait for the general public window to unlock.

Dodge third-party sellers — Double-check the seller before buying. Marketplace scalpers frequently list units for jacked-up prices; make sure it states "Sold and shipped by [Retailer]" at the standard price.

Sources indicate that skip the web wars and head to physical stores — Online checkout bots grab website stock in under 15 seconds. Showing up in person is easily your most reliable path to securing one without paying scalper markups.

Bartesian is the Keurig of cocktails. After trying several automatic cocktail makers on the market, it was the only cocktail maker I could see fitting into my normal routine. It works like any capsule-style device, but with booze. You fill the Bartesian’s glass bottles with your liquor of choice, make sure there’s water in the reservoir, plop in a cocktail capsule (these typically cost $2-3), choose your drink strength, press “mix,” and then a drink comes out. (If you’ve got kids, the Bartesian Professional version comes with a lock that will stymie curious fingers.).

Recent findings suggest that do you need a Bartesian to make cocktails? Of course you don’t. You can dump tequila into sour mix anytime and call it a margarita. But perhaps you’d like to make an espresso martini, a blackberry margarita, and also a Long Island Iced Tea? The Bartesian is a sort of shortcut to a home bar, without having to store all the mixers—and a bit of a novelty. It will be fun, and silly, and the drinks are kind of fine in a Spring Break way: strong and sweet and with sometimes fun flavors. Don’t expect sophistication. Expect a bit of a party trick, the sort of thing that makes a summer a little more fun.

Bao Fan, 52, started the boutique investment bank in 2005 and has been unreachable since the middle of February, according to the organization. Shares in China Renaissance have plunged since Bao went missing, at one point dropping as much as 50%.

It has been revealed that china Renaissance said in late February that it had learned Bao was “cooperating in an investigation” being carried out by certain authorities in the country. It gave no other details.

Chinese media have reported Bao might be assisting in an investigation related to a former executive at China Renaissance.

In a filing on Sunday, China Renaissance said auditors couldn’t complete their work or sign off on their report because of Bao’s absence. The board was also unable to give an estimate about when it would be able to approve its audited results for 2022 or dispatch its annual report by an April 30 deadline as required by Hong Kong’s listing rules.

Missing Chinese billionaire CEO assisting authorities in investigation, company notes.

Trading in the organization’s shares was suspended from Monday as a result.

Industry observers note that bao is known as a veteran dealmaker who works closely with top technology companies in China. He helped broker the 2015 merger between two of the country’s leading food delivery services, Meituan and Dianping. Today, the combined organization’s “super app” platform is ubiquitous in China.

His team has also invested in US-listed Chinese electric vehicle makers Nio (NIO) and Li Auto and helped Chinese internet giants Baidu (BIDU) and JD.com (JD) complete their secondary listings in Hong Kong.

Recent findings suggest that over the weekend, China’s top anti-graft watchdog debuted an investigation into Liu Liange, former party secretary and chairman of Bank of China, according to a statement by the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection and the State Supervision Commission. The bank is state-owned and one of the country’s four biggest lenders.

Liu is suspected of “serious violations of discipline and law,” the statement mentioned. He is among the most senior financial executives targeted in a broader financial crackdown by President Xi Jinping.

In January, Wang Bin, former party chief and chairman of China Life Insurance, was charged by national-level prosecutors with taking bribes and hiding overseas savings.

Palace docked points for using four sub windows in WSL win

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (589 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Scottish striker Kirsty Howat signed for Crystal Palace in September 2025.
  • Crystal Palace have been deducted three points after using too many substitution windows during their win on the opening day of the 2026-27 Women's Super League season.
  • Palace, who were playing their first match following promotion back to the WSL, beat Everton 1-0 on 6 September at Gander Green Lane.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scottish striker Kirsty Howat signed for Crystal Palace in September 2025.

Crystal Palace have been deducted three points after using too many substitution windows during their win on the opening day of the 2026-27 Women's Super League season.

Palace, who were playing their first match following promotion back to the WSL, beat Everton 1-0 on 6 September at Gander Green Lane.

However, manager Jo Potter brought on Kirsty Howat for Shannon O'Brien in the seventh minute of second-half stoppage time to try and shore up the victory.

It was the fourth separate substitution made by Potter, who had also made changes in the 62nd, 83rd and 90th minutes.

While WSL managers are allowed to make five changes in a game, they must be made across only three stoppages in play to avoid excessive time wasting.

Crystal Palace deducted points following WSL win.

Palace have been stripped of the three points they earned in the match - one of only two WSL games the Eagles have won this season.

This punishment drops Palace down one place in the WSL table to 13th - the relegation play-off place.

Palace are now below fellow promoted side Birmingham City in the table on goal difference, with both sides now having six points - six behind Everton in 11th.

In a statement on their club website, external Palace stated they were "disappointed" by the decision.

The decision was made by an independent tribunal after Palace admitted the breach of competition rule 5.19.1.

It has been revealed that the rule states: "A substitution can only be made when play is stopped for any reason and the referee has given permission. A club at its discretion may use five substitute players during a match. For the avoidance of doubt, each club has no more than three substitution opportunities in each match.".

The tribunal remarked that while the rule breach was inadvertent and "not intended to secure an unfair advantage", it said a points deduction was necessary in order to provide a deterrent to clubs against making a similar mistake in future.

"The integrity of the competition would be damaged if a club that had breached the rules on substitution opportunities, and had won the match, were allowed to keep the points it obtained, save in exceptional circumstances," the tribunal stated in its full written decision., external.

They stated the lateness of the substitution in the match - so late that Howat did not touch the ball after coming on - did not excuse Palace from punishment.

It also ruled "that responsibility for complying with the rule rests with clubs, not match officials".

Palace - who placed the word "fourth" in inverted commas in their response to the ruling - are aiming to improve on their only previous WSL campaign in 2024-25, where they only won twice in 22 matches and were relegated by a 10-point margin.

Their statement read: "Everyone at the club is obviously frustrated that such a minor infraction, given that the player was on the pitch for only 46 seconds while the ball was in play, has led to such a significant penalty â a penalty which we do not agree is reasonable or proportionate.

"We are disappointed for the players and staff who worked so hard to secure a deserved victory on our return to the WSL.".

Forward Lexi Lloyd-Smith had scored the only goal of the game in the 34th minute on her Palace debut.

Find interviews and extra content on the BBC Women's Football Weekly feed.

According to recent reports, shailene Woodley’s early 20s were not an easy time health-wise.“It got to the point where I was losing my hearing. I couldn’t walk for longer than five minutes at a time without having to lay down for hours, and hours and sleep. Everything I ate hurt my stomach,” the actress mentioned on a September 2024 episode of the SHE MD Podcast. “It was this conflation of problems and diagnoses and different doctors telling me different things.”So Shailene—who chose to keep the exact condition private—set out to find answers. “I come from a very holistic background and study herbalism,” she added. “So I was very keen on, ‘I’m going to work with real MDs, [and] I’m also going to work with independent kind of healers.’ Just trying to search for some sense of comfort in my own skin.”It was a long journey—one that lasted for 10 years.“Throughout that decade, a lot of other things came from feeling so much discomfort physically,” the Substantial Little Lies star noted, “which was, ‘My gosh, if everything I eat hurts my stomach, I’m now suddenly afraid of food.’ And then going into the kind of mental f--ckery that can happen with that of body dysmorphia and confusion about identity and feeling safe in my own capsule, in my own skin, what that meant, and what that should be.”After tending to both her physical and mental health, Shailene is feeling much better.“It was a journey that ultimately physically resolved itself, and I am very healthy,” she shared. “I’m so happy to be able to say that.".

Check physical stores in the morning: Online checkout bots can wipe out digital inventory in seconds. Visiting Target, Best Buy, or GameStop right when doors open often turns up fresh shipment boxes that never made it onto website listings.

Latest Update: Yoro red card overturned, but refs' chief Webb backs decision

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (952 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Leny Yoro was sent off for this tackle on Alexander Isak.
  • Manchester United defender Leny Yoro has had the red card shown to him at Anfield overturned by the Football Association - even though referees' chief Howard Webb has backed the decision to send the defender off.
  • Yoro was dismissed by referee Sam Barrott for bringing down Liverpool forward Alexander Isak just eight minutes into Sunday's match.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Leny Yoro was sent off for this tackle on Alexander Isak.

Manchester United defender Leny Yoro has had the red card shown to him at Anfield overturned by the Football Association - even though referees' chief Howard Webb has backed the decision to send the defender off.

Yoro was dismissed by referee Sam Barrott for bringing down Liverpool forward Alexander Isak just eight minutes into Sunday's match.

Isak had run onto a ball that bounced over Matthijs de Ligt but took a heavy touch that meant the ball was likely to run through to United goalkeeper Senne Lammens even if Yoro had not brought down the Swede.

Fresh United head coach Mauricio Pochettino was furious at a decision he felt had changed the course of the game, which Liverpool won 4-0.

Industry observers note that "The ball wasn't in his control," he said. "Isak, when he saw the control wasn't good, it's normal to delay, and stop to the run. In that moment that Yoro came from the back, and you go down.

"But all that we play football; you know that wasn't intentional. That is never a foul.".

The FA backed that view, meaning Yoro will be clear to face Brentford in the Premier League at Old Trafford on Saturday.

However, in the latest edition of Mic'd Up on Sky Sports, Webb mentioned Barrott got it right.

"I think, by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving promptly on towards that ball," he said.

'No-one's coming to save us' - but how can Man Utd save themselves?

How on earth can the head of referees say a decision was right, but the FA say it was wrong?

According to recent reports, "The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it's a little bit debatable," Webb said. "Certainly not clearly wrong.".

Not clearly and obviously wrong for a VAR intervention, but clearly and obviously wrong for the FA to rescind the red card.

You wonder how the general fan is supposed to understand it all.

The FA's appeals process is notoriously difficult to predict, especially on highly borderline situations like Yoro.

A commission features three people, usually former players though sometimes there is a retired official is on the panel.

A simple majority is needed, so a club just needs two people to agree with them.

It's why clubs might appeal against red cards when it seems impossible to win, you just never know.

Such was the split of opinion on Yoro, United always stood a chance of at least getting those key two votes.

And this is the crux of appeals process. An FA commission is just the subjective opinion of three people.

Do the appeal again tomorrow with three different panel members, and United might lose.

This is why Pro Ref don't use the outcome of FA appeals to determine how games are officiated.

It has been revealed that two years ago, Brentford's Christian Norgaard won an appeal against a red card at Everton. That was a split 2:1 vote, but enough to say a decision was wrong.

Pro Ref told its referees not to alter their interpretation based on this vote.

In a recent development, let's throw in another one. The Premier League's Key Match Incidents Panel.

Earlier this season, Brighton appealed against Pascal Struijk's VAR red card at Sunderland.

An FA commission upheld the appeal, but in contradiction the KMI Panel voted the VAR intervention was correct.

Make it make sense, supporters might ask.

This will forever be the problem with officiating, and indeed any hope of true consistency with VAR.

Was Yoro's red card right or wrong? On which side of the fence will the KMI Panel fall?

In a recent development, football is just a floating mass of subjectivity. Of referees, of VARs, of panel members and of fans. It just depends whose opinion you ask.

Sporting coach Paulo Fonseca speaks to the media ahead of the Champions League clash with Manchester United.

United have travelled to Lisbon for their next Champions League match on Wednesday (20:00 GMT).

The early dismissal of Yoro at Anfield meant Sporting had no chance to assess any changes Pochettino might have made after he replaced Michael Carrick during the international break.

But despite United sitting 19th in the Premier League, Sporting boss refuses to accept United are "fragile".

"I don't following the reasoning," said Fonseca, who was only appointed on 4 November after the Portuguese club bought him out of his contract at Lyon.

In a recent development, "Manchester is a great team," he said. "I don't believe a lot that great teams are fragile. The last game they played in the Champions League, they were trailing 2-0, then won 3-2 against a very difficult opponent in Roma.

"Moreover, when they have a latest head coach, with such world-class players, it's extremely unpredictable to see if they will have a good day or bad day.".

United have not won in the Premier League since August and have conceded 19 goals in their past six games in all competitions.

Yet, such was the nature of the Liverpool game, Fonseca has had to watch analysis of Pochettino's time in charge of the United States to get an idea of what to expect.

It has been revealed that "Eight minutes, red card. It's impossible to make an analysis," he noted.

"I tried to see Pochettino with the United States and what kind of solutions he used. There is some information but it is very difficult to predict.".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, the Goodforces wants to help make that a reality with their campaign neunund20 (twenty-nine), taking its cue, in part, from the American left.
  • Co-founder Patrick Haermeyer told DW that the campaign's aim is "to give people hope and an alternative narrative to: Things are getting worse and worse." He worked as an online organizer for the election team of Bernie Sanders in the US Democratic presidential primaries in 2016 and cites Sanders' "not me, us" campaign as an inspiration.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that red, red, green — those are the party colors of the left-leaning coalition recently formed in the German state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. Now a Berlin-based agency wants to see the same alliance between the center-left Social Democrats, the socialist Left Party, and environmentalist Greens win the 2029 national elections.

In a recent development, the Goodforces wants to help make that a reality with their campaign neunund20 (twenty-nine), taking its cue, in part, from the American left. The agency was set up in response to the rise of the far right across Europe.

Co-founder Patrick Haermeyer told DW that the campaign's aim is "to give people hope and an alternative narrative to: Things are getting worse and worse." He worked as an online organizer for the election team of Bernie Sanders in the US Democratic presidential primaries in 2016 and cites Sanders' "not me, us" campaign as an inspiration.

Neunund20 currently has two strategies: It provides digital space for short-form videos and social media content on political and social topics on Instagram, Tiktok, and Bluesky. At the same time, it tries to connect content creators, activists, NGOs, and political initiatives around shared "progressive" issues.

Industry observers note that users with a particular interest can click to get a link giving them access to archives of relevant social media material that they can then reshare. That feature is modelled on the campaign of New York's left-wing mayor Zohran Mamdani.

It has been revealed that and there are other projects. The Goodforces was recently involved in a tactical voting initiative in the September elections in the state of Saxony-Anhalt, intended to keep the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) from winning an absolute majority. Haermeyer states physical campaigns of that kind are necessary to provide essential "interim victories" en route to the next parliamentary elections.

The Greens and the SPD, the two parties recommended by the app created by the organization, made it over the 5% hurdle and into parliament. The help that they received was declared by each party in the form of a €40,000 ($43,900) donation.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The agency sees itself as a kind of Super PAC, modeled on political organizations in the United States that collect money to carry out campaigns without directly supporting a single party or a special candidate.

For Christoph Bieber, political scientist at the University of Duisburg-Essen, the Goodforces is an interesting upcoming type of player on Germany's political scene because it operates outside the country's political parties.

But many of those parties are eyeing the development with disquiet. The far-left, populist, immigration skeptical Alliance for Social Justice and Economic Reason (BSW) criticized the Goodforces' intervention in Saxony-Anhalt, telling the newspaper FAZ that it was an "infantilizing, and perhaps even antidemocratic action." The neoliberal Free Democrats (FDP) called the tool "wrong and intentionally misleading." The FDP failed to clear the threshold, while the BSW only just squeaked in. The AfD gained 43% of the vote and its candidate may soon become Germany's first far-right state premier since the Nazi era.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

It has been revealed that haermeyer set up the agency in 2024 along with Peter Jelinek, and both men previously worked for Green Party European Parliament member Michael Bloss. Ahead of that year's European elections, the EU's Green Deal began to come under increasing attack.

That year also ended with the collapse of Germany's first federal coalition between the SPD, Greens, and FDP, after much infighting and attacks from right-wing quarters.

"We noticed that more and more successes and freedoms that we had fought for were being reversed: Things like freedom of movement, border checks, and other things that were coming more and more under fire," Haermeyer told DW. "And we noticed that it was primarily democratic and progressive forces that were being drawn into defensive battles.".

According to recent reports, the AfD, founded in 2013, already in the age of social media, has successfully targeted younger voters with in its online campaigns. But the older parties, in particular, have struggled. The Goodforces saw a need for support in the online environment and is now seeking to plug this gap.

Sources indicate that the social media accounts of the campaign neunund20 contain posts on domestic German topics, such as the current negotiations to form a red-red-green coalition government in Berlin, and the country's upcoming military service law. They also highlight "wins" in Spain in the protests for affordable housing and for US Democrats in the midterms.

Haermeyer stresses that the issues the agency highlights are determined together with a wide range of grassroots organizations and activists. "The campaign is not agreed in conjunction with the SPD, the Left Party, and the Greens," he said.

Sources indicate that agency funding comes from commissions and small donations. Haermeyer says that contributions generally range from $20 to $50.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Bieber sees the emergence of non-party campaigning, long an accepted practice in the US, as a bid to compensate for the shortcomings of traditional parties.

"It is an omission of the parties," he noted. "For years they have been saying we have to modernize, we have to become more open and get away from rigid membership structures. There are legal regulations governing the organization of political parties in Germany, but perhaps it could be more flexible and open.".

According to recent reports, the center-left and center-right big-tent parties have been in decline for decades. Membership of the SPD dropped from 943,000 in 1990 to some 348,000 at the end of 2025. Chancellor Friedrich Merz's Christian Democratic Union (CDU) has seen a fall from 750,000 to under 357,000.

It has been revealed that party membership is particularly low in former communist eastern Germany. Centrist parties have also struggled to attract younger voters. A report by the Deutsche Kinder und Jugendstiftung (German Children and Youth Foundation) indicated that only 20% of young people felt their concerns were taken seriously in the 2025 German elections and that trust in parties was low.

Sources indicate that in the United States, campaign financing comes predominantly from donations, and lobby groups can buy influence by contributing unlimited amounts to super PACs. In Germany, party funding comes, in part, from taxpayers and membership fees, and donations are capped. However, Bieber warns that whereas there are strict rules regarding the disclosure of donors to US Super PACs, these do not exist in Germany.

The political scientist does not believe that US-style campaigning is going to take hold in Germany, but he does see potential dangers: "This could be a door opener to make others consider whether they want to go in this direction in the field of campaigning. And he added: "If it becomes rife, it could lead to a further devaluation of parties and their structures.".

Seeking redemption after failing at Spurs, newly installed Crystal Palace manager has a tough challenge ahead.

Thomas Frank promised his wife, Nanna, he would take a year’s sabbatical after being sacked by Tottenham in February, but he couldn’t wait that long. Having received a reported £8m payoff from Spurs, he kept an extremely low profile in the first few months after an experience at the club that sources close to the 53‑year‑old have described as “traumatic”.

Frank broke his silence at the start of June with a statement released by the League Managers Association. It said he would cover the World Cup for the BBC (thereby going head-to-head with Ange Postecoglou, his predecessor at Spurs, who worked for ITV) before “experiencing the Tour de France”, a lifelong passion. Frank usually preferred to run to Brentford’s training ground and home matches from his home in East Sheen during a nine‑year spell as assistant and then manager, but he occasionally cycled because it helped to clear his head.

Dancing With the Stars' Derek Hough Details Childhood Abuse

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1754 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eonline

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As the Dancing With the Stars judge looked back on the beginning of his path to becoming a professional dancer, he shared one of the darker chapters of his childhood with sister Julianne Hough while being raised in the suburbs of Salt Lake City, Utah.
  • "The neighborhood that we grew up in, we definitely just had some neighbors that weren't great.
  • In addition, the 41-year-old explained of the traumatic period, "They hung me up in a tree by my ankles, put a gun to my head, spat on me, hogtied me up in a field and left me there.".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Derek Hough healed through dance.

As the Dancing With the Stars judge looked back on the beginning of his path to becoming a professional dancer, he shared one of the darker chapters of his childhood with sister Julianne Hough while being raised in the suburbs of Salt Lake City, Utah.

"The neighborhood that we grew up in, we definitely just had some neighbors that weren't great. They pretty much terrorized my family in a lot of ways," Derek shared in his Nov. 23 documentary Symphony of Dance per USA Today, stating, "One of my neighbors was, for lack of a better word, just really inappropriate with me physically.".

In addition, the 41-year-old explained of the traumatic period, "They hung me up in a tree by my ankles, put a gun to my head, spat on me, hogtied me up in a field and left me there.".

As such, enduring the abuse led to "a lot of emotion" for the then-12-year-old, who was raised alongside his DWTS costar as well as their older siblings Sharee, 49, Marabeth, 45 and Katherine, 44, by parents Bruce Hough and Mariann Heaton in the Mormon community. Julianne has previously shared that a painful part of her upbringing came at the hands of a neighbor in their cul-de-sac who she noted sexually abused her at age 4.

"I just didn't understand where I was going," Derek said in the Hulu project about his reaction to the harmful treatment. "I was kind of left to my own devices.".

And at first, the trauma pushed the choreographer further away from his future as a ballroom pro.

Recent findings suggest that as he detailed, "I was a 12-year-old. I would skip school. I would skip dance. I wouldn't go. My dad was at work, and my mom was off, and [I was] just floating around with no direction.".

Fortunately, Derek was "relieved" when he met mentors Corky Ballas and Shirley Ballas—parents of DWTS coach Mark Ballas—who soon moved Derek, and eventually Julianne, to London to attend drama academy Italia Conti Academy of Theatre Arts.

In a recent development, "Moving away was great because I was getting away from something," he mentioned. "I was leaving this wounded boy, and I was gonna go become this success. I was gonna go work hard and achieve things and overcome things.".

According to recent reports, and the Emmy winner did exactly that, noting how the professional performers in his new world made him realize at the time, "This is what I want to do. I want to be like these guys.".

Julianne alluded to her siblings undergoing hardship similar to her own on The Jamie Kern Lima Show Aug. 15 while telling her story, noting, "By the way, I'm not the only one in my family that had gone through similar things, so that was a very challenging thing to come to terms with.".

Read on for a closer look at the Hough family tree.

The Hough family patriarch is originally from Coeur d’Alene, Idaho, and met future wife Mariann Heaton on the ballroom team at Ricks College (now Brigham Young University-Idaho).

Bruce and Mariann—both from Mormon families and the children of ballroom-dancing parents—settled in Salt Lake City. There he worked as a communications executive and co-founded supplement maker Nutraceutical Corporation, which, according to Deseret News, reached a valuation of $300 million under his watch before it was sold in 2017.

Bruce also ventured into politics, serving two terms as state Republican Party chair and running for congress in 2023.

While he didn't win that race, he told Deseret News at the time that he was running for his family's future. "I’ve got 10 kids, I’ve got 22 grandkids and growing," he explained. "And I really feel that America’s promise is in jeopardy for those grandkids especially.".

Of his most famous offspring, he quipped, "I never thought that those dance lessons would pay off,” noting that he took the most pride in hearing from others that son Derek Hough and daughter Julianne Hough were some of the "kindest people…in the entertainment business.”.

In addition to Derek and Julianne, Bruce shares daughters Sharee Hough Selman, Marabeth Poole and Katherine Hough with Mariann. After they divorced in the late 1990s, he married Debra Francom Hough, also a parent of five.

Mariann grew up in Idaho Falls with three brothers.

She and Bruce were in the process of divorcing when Julianne and Derek, then 10 and 13, moved to London to attend the Italia Conti Academy of Theatre Arts.

Their leaving was "devastating," Mariann recalled on a 2019 episode of The Minds Gym podcast. But they wanted to dance and, she explained, "The biggest thing that kept me going is that I grew up feeling very dominated over and controlled. Love my parents, but that was like a generational thing.".

However, she added, "I'm grateful for that now because…it made me sway to I love having free agency." It was also "so important" for her to pass that on to her kids, she mentioned, and "all of them are so not afraid to go travel and do all these things.".

Mariann, now based in Franklin, Tenn., is a painter and has credited husband Aaron Nelson for supporting and encouraging her work as an artist.

Sharee married husband Mark Selman when she was 19 and they share six kids.

The eldest of Bruce and Mariann's brood danced at Ballet West in Utah and these days runs her own fitness business, Hough Werks, teaching yoga and dance.

Her "dynamic" firstborn "just came into this world with a lot of energy," Mariann noted on The Minds Gym. Sharee's "little mind was just going all the time, just super creative" and "self-motivated.".

Moreover, with 11 years between Sharee and her youngest sister, "Julianne thinks she has two moms.".

Marabeth is "just a beautiful spirit" who "loves her own space," Mariann mentioned of her second child, and she "puts on these little retreats in Nashville for women.".

She left Utah for Music City to "be a country star," baby sister Julianne shared on the Not Skinny but Not Fat podcast in September 2025, and now makes the most of her positive energy as a realtor and holistic health coach, as well as a singer-songwriter.

Marabeth married Michael Poole in 2002 and they live in Nashville with son Aidan.

Daughter Katherine, a mother of three, "just makes you smile," Mariann said on The Minds Gym, "and she's just real.".

Sources indicate that the esthetician was in a relationship with Tony Schnur before his death from brain cancer in 2023. "It’s unfair that I found my soulmate, my best friend, my partner in life, only to lose you too soon," Katherine posted on Instragram in February 2025, marking the second anniversary of his passing. "I miss you every day.".

But Katherine has persevered, Julianne gushing on Not Skinny But Not Fat, "She has three beautiful daughters and she has all these activities and she plans all these things, and I'm in awe of her.".

And on Sept. 24, 2025, Katherine shared that she had found love again, writing on Instagram alongside a montage of sweet photos, "After walking through so much loss and heartache, I never imagined I’d find this kind of love again. Chris is the man I prayed for, kind, generous, loving, patient, and such a gift not only to me but to my girls.".

Born May 17, 1985, Derek joined Dancing With the Stars as a pro in 2007. He won the Mirrorball Trophy a record six times and is a four-time Emmy winner for choreography.

After his last competitive turn around the floor in 2016, Derek returned to DWTS as a fulltime judge in 2020.

He met fellow dancer Hayley Erbert in 2015 and, after navigating some "insane obstacles," as he put it on Couple Things With Shawn Johnson and Andrew East, they got married in August 2023.

As a couple they powered through Hayley's life-threatening health scare, a brain hemorrhage that required emergency surgery just four months after their wedding, and in July 2025 they announced they were expecting their first child together.

Posting a photo of dad Bruce dancing at his and Hayley's wedding, Derek wrote on Facebook in April 2024, "Smart, kind and thoughtful. I hope to be as good as a father as he has been to his family.".

According to recent reports, the baby of the Hough family was born July 20,1988. She joined DWTS in 2007 along with Derek and proceeded to win her first two seasons on the show.

It has been revealed that she left in 2009 to pursue acting and scored a breakthrough role in 2010's Burlesque (though her substantial-screen debut was actually playing an unnamed Hogwarts student in 2001's Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone) before scoring the lead in the 2011 Footloose remake. Julianne returned to the ballroom as a judge from 2014 to 2017, winning an Emmy for choreography along the way, and has cohosted DWTS with Alfonso Ribeiro since 2023.

Julianne married Brooks Laich in 2017 but they split up in 2020, eventually finalizing their divorce in 2022.

She stated on The Jamie Kern Lima Show in 2024 that going through a divorce gave her a chance to "reconnect" with her mom and dad, and they "showed up" for her.

Industry observers note that "I needed that," Julianne explained. "I reclaimed my parental relationship with them and I got to be the kid and they got to take care of me. And that was the most healing [thing].".

Reflecting on her and Derek becoming the stars of the family, Julianne said on Not Skinny But Not Fat that there was "no jealousy" between their other siblings, "but there is a sadness that maybe there wasn't an opportunity for them to experience it.".

Sharee, Marabeth and Katherine are "so, so, so happy," Julianne continued. "They have great lives, and they love their life. But we had an opportunity that they didn't have, and it's hard.”.

And while she and Derek have a special connection, "they were super close as sisters growing up,” Julianne mentioned. “So, I didn't get to have the closeness of sisters and that bond. [And] they have marriages and kids and I don't have that experience.".

Meanwhile, all five siblings "get along really well," Mariann mentioned on The Minds Gym. "I think the hard part is being away from each other, because there is some kind of a synergy when they all get together.".

The journalist and broadcaster who died last week aged 69 knew the enduring power of radio, even as the landscape changed so quickly.

It has been revealed that it’s injury time at the Emirates on 29 October 2008, Arsenal are 4-3 up against Tottenham. Tom Huddlestone cushions a ball to Luka Modric, whose strike takes a deflection. It loops over Manuel Almunia and off a post into the path of Aaron Lennon, who prods it home and starts skipping towards the Spurs supporters before diving on to the ground and being enveloped by Modric, Benoît Assou-Ekotto, Darren Bent and a couple of pitch-invading fans. Pandemonium, for once, seems the apt way to describe it.

According to recent reports, but the real entertainment is happening in a radio studio at 18 Hatfields, London SE1; the old home of TalkSport. As the goal goes in, a guttural voice makes an indecipherable but very loud noise. It’s hard to transcribe – perhaps “ERRRRRAAAARRRGGHH”, or maybe “OOEEERRAAGGH”. It’s just a noise, but it’s unmistakably Danny Kelly. He regains the power of speech and follows it up with: “Gooooaaaal … Goalll Stan, Goalll at the Emirates.” Reporter Ian Abrahams and Stan Collymore join the excitement, before Danny comes back: “I LOVE FOOTBALL, STAN, I LOVE IT.” It is such a brilliant piece of radio. From one of the absolute greats.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fiona first rose to fame when she was born premature at Cincinnati Zoo in 2017.

Major League Soccer side FC Cincinnati will honour Fiona, a hippo that recently died at the city's zoo, with a tifo display at their match with Nashville SC on Saturday.

Fiona, a social media star since her premature birth at the zoo in 2017, died on Thursday after swallowing a woollen hat that had slipped into her enclosure.

The Ohio side will now raise a banner depicting the nine-year-old semi-aquatic mammal in their post-season MLS Cup encounter with Nashville, who won the Supporters' Shield for being the highest-placed team in the league campaign.

Cincinnati noted Fiona was a "beloved hippo who became a symbol of Cincinnati and captured hearts around the world".

The tifo will be produced by fan group The Forge Cincy, who painted the display on Sunday in a garage next to Cincinnati's TQL Stadium.

The club will also make a donation in Fiona's memory for every fan in attendance to the Cincinnati Zoo and Botanical Garden.

Fan group The Forge Cincy had previously spent two weeks creating a tifo for their "Hell is Real" October derby match against Ohio rivals Columbus.

Removal of hat inside Fiona the hippo was 'impossible', Cincinnati Zoo says.

Fiona the hippo dies after swallowing a hat at Cincinnati Zoo.

Cincinnati's Nick Hagglund, who hails from the city and is in his eighth season with the team, previously paid tribute to Fiona after scoring in his side's 3-1 victory over Orlando on the day of her death.

The defender yelled "that's for Fiona", mimicking the ears on top of her head, in a celebration video, external on the club's Instagram.

Later, on his Instagram account, external, Hagglund posted, "This one was for her @fionahippo @cincinnatizoo.

"Cincinnati needed a win on the day after the passing of our beloved hippo, a symbol of hope and resilience for our city, and the lads answered the call.".

Cincinnati's tifo is one of a number of tributes paid to the hippo, with Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins wearing a Fiona sweater, external prior to his American football franchise's defeat by the Washington Commanders on Monday.

Meanwhile handlers of the blue hippo balloon at Upcoming York's annual Macy's Thanksgiving Parade will wear a purple patch in her honour.

At birth, Fiona weighed 13kg (29lb), which the zoo noted was about half the previous lowest recorded birth weight for her species, and she previously inspired an ice cream flavour and a character in Cincinnati's ballet.

From premature baby to social media star - famed Cincinnati Zoo hippo Fiona dies.

Fiona swallowed the woollen hat around 10 days prior to her death, with the item getting into her enclosure by accident after a visitor tossed it in the air and it caught on a ceiling fan that flung it through a small opening.

"We probably couldn't make [it] happen again if we tried," noted zoo spokesperson Michelle Curley.

Hippos normally live up to 50 years in human care, according to the zoo.

Nashville finished top of the MLS Eastern Conference, 31 points ahead of ninth-placed Cincinnati.

However, having beaten Orlando in a one-off wildcard round, Cincinnati defeated Nashville 1-0 in the opening match of their best-of-three round one series.

Should Cincinnati win on Saturday they will progress to a one-off conference semi-final with either Chicago Fire or Charlotte FC, with a conference final prior to the season-ending MLS Cup final.

Tom Brady knows that all parents drop the ball sometimes.

Since becoming dad to son Jack, 19, with ex-girlfriend Bridget Moynahan, as well as son Benjamin, 16, and daughter Vivian, 13, with ex-wife Gisele Bündchen, the seven-time Super Bowl champ admitted there are some losses among his many wins as a parent.

“Well, I’ve made a lot of mistakes,” Brady stated on the Nov. 22 episode of the High Performance podcast. “So, a lot like quarterback. I threw a lot of interceptions. And with every one I’ve tried to learn.”.

It has been revealed that and with that effort, the 49-year-old added, “I hope I’m a better parent today than I was when I first started having kids. And hopefully I’m a better parent 10 years from now.”.

So, what is Brady’s game blueprint for becoming the best dad he can be?

According to recent reports, “The important thing for me in my personal life is to go where my kids are at, too,” he explained. “Not to say, ‘Hey kids, pay attention to the things I'm doing or what's important to me.’ It’s been a really important lesson for me over the years to go to my kids and say, ‘What’s really important to you? What’s driving you? Or what are you scared of, or how can I pay attention to the things that you value?’”.

Finding ways to connect with his kids is a skill Brady said he developed from leading football teams during his 23 seasons as an NFL quarterback.

“Part of that is just being really open and present and also trying to be really relatable to the younger [generation],” he continued, “which I was very fortunate to learn over the course of my playing career.”.

And now, Brady emphasized that he is simply trying to be “really present” and “non-judgmental” with his kids while imparting the wisdom he’s scored through his “years of experience.”.

As he put it, he is “just trying to understand their perspective, but also trying to get them to understand my perspective a little bit, too.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of light.
  • Rømer disproved this almost by accident when he was studying Jupiter's moon Io.
  • Industry observers note that to his surprise, the timing of the eclipses was not consistent.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of light. Before Rømer figured it out, scientists thought that light travels instantaneously, or infinitely fast.

Rømer disproved this almost by accident when he was studying Jupiter's moon Io. He was trying to figure out how long it takes Io to orbit Jupiter in hopes of using it as a cosmic clock. He watched Io disappear behind Jupiter and reappear on the other side. He did this over and over every 42 hours for years.

Industry observers note that to his surprise, the timing of the eclipses was not consistent. When Earth was closest to Jupiter, the eclipses happened 11 minutes early. Likewise, when the two planets were farthest away, the eclipses were 11 minutes behind schedule.

Industry observers note that rømer figured out the pattern and made an accurate prediction for Io's eclipse on Nov. 9, 1676. Then on Nov. 21, he took his findings to the Royal Academy of Sciences and explained that a finite speed of light must be responsible.

According to recent reports, understanding that the speed of light is a constant is the key that opened our ability to gauge the scale of the universe, as well as was central to developing modern physics."The speed of light becomes a sort of ultimate speed limit," Live Science explained in an article about why the speed of light matters. "In fact, objects with mass, be they cars or neutrinos, can't reach the speed of light because they would need infinite energy to do so.".

Sources indicate that on this day in space! Nov. 20, 1998: Russia debuts 1st module of International Space Station as construction begins on the largest human-built structure in orbit.

Sources indicate that hanneke Weitering is a multimedia journalist in the Pacific Northwest reporting on the future of aviation at FutureFlight.aero and Aviation International News and was previously the Editor for Spaceflight and Astronomy news here at Space.com. As an editor with over 10 years of experience in science journalism she has previously written for Scholastic Classroom Magazines, MedPage Today and The Joint Institute for Computational Sciences at Oak Ridge National Laboratory. After studying physics at the University of Tennessee in her hometown of Knoxville, she earned her graduate degree in Science, Health and Environmental Reporting (SHERP) from New York University. Hanneke joined the Space.com team in 2016 as a staff writer and producer, covering topics including spaceflight and astronomy. She currently lives in Seattle, home of the Space Needle, with her cat and two snakes. In her spare time, Hanneke enjoys exploring the Rocky Mountains, basking in nature and looking for dark skies to gaze at the cosmos.

Audiophiles and custom equalizer fans: After three years, Sony's flagship wireless headphones finally got an update. If you love Sony headphones and have an old pair of XM4s, then we can definitely recommend an upgrade. However, if you just purchased a pair of XM5s, then it might be harder to justify an instant upgrade. That remarked, the active noise cancellation is better than ever, and there are noticeable improvements to audio quality (even if they lose out by a smidge to the latest Technics AZ100 earbuds). Besides music lovers, travelers will also appreciate the fresh Sony cans, as they fold up and come with an improved travel case.

According to recent reports, mashable's Tech Editor Timothy Beck Werth reviewed the XM6 headphones ahead of their launch, and he was impressed with the overall quality. As Werth wrote in his review, "The latest Sony headphones offer impressive audio quality, and they definitely improve on the XM5 models.
