Senegal won January’s final 1-0 after walking off.

Result was overturned in March as 3-0 win for Morocco.

Senegal have been reinstated as the champions of Africa, and their controversial 1-0 victory against Morocco confirmed in the record books, after the scandal over January’s Africa Cup of Nations final was resolved in a Swiss courtroom.

The court of arbitration for sport (Cas) ruled that a decision to award the 2025 Afcon title to Morocco on appeal should be set aside. Senegal celebrated with a social media post proclaiming the team to have won the title twice: first on the field and then at Cas. Morocco, who are due to co-host the World Cup in 2030, declared their intention to “pursue all legal avenues” to challenge the ruling.

Jamal Musiala has started one Bundesliga game this season.

Bayern Munich are only focused on getting Jamal Musiala back from injury and are not interested in the comments made regarding his contract, the club's sporting director Max Eberl insisted.

The 23-year-old collapsed twice in four days during pre-season and remarked he had been diagnosed with "easily treatable absence seizures, which are due to a neurological dysfunction".

Last week, players' union Fifpro said Bayern Munich's hierarchy "should know better" after the club's honorary president Uli Hoeness said the midfielder may never "regain the performance level he once had".

Describing the talks on Tuesday as "very, very constructive", Eberl mentioned the focus was on Musiala's recovery from a recent injury.

"Today it was about just how we want to get Jamal back on the field, just like before his muscle injury in the international break," Eberl said.

"That's the only task FC Bayern has right now, to give Jamal this trust and not some topics about money or something.".

The Bundesliga club's chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen questioned the lucrative contract extension the Germany international signed in 2025, running until 2030, if Musiala fails to get back to his best form, while his predecessor Karl-Heinz Rummenigge suggested the deal, external may need to be renegotiated.

Bayern manager Vincent Kompany mentioned in September it wouldn't be "a substantial deal" if the seizures return.

Musiala, previously a regular starter and one of the best young talents in Europe, has played five times this season, scoring twice.

Recent findings suggest that "Contracts are there to be respected," Fifpro stated on Saturday. "An injury or a dip in form gives a club no grounds to reopen terms it agreed to, just as a run of outstanding performances gives a player no automatic right to a pay rise.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, if you're looking for a latest pair of earbuds, we have good news: You have a lot of options. The bad news? You have a lot of options, and your decision can get overwhelming, fast. Wasn't life easier when iPhones came with a free pair of earbuds?

It has been revealed that while you can still find wired earbuds that plug in and go, the market is flooded with high-quality wireless options. Now, you'll find models with advanced active noise cancellation, multi-point pairing, high-resolution audio support, and extra-long battery life. To help you choose, Mashable's audio experts put the best wireless earbuds from Apple, Bose, Sony, and other top brands to the test.

These are the tech, tools, and products — from laptops to e-readers, from earbuds to robovacs, and more — that Mashable ranks best in class.

Recent findings suggest that the best wireless earbuds range anywhere from $10 to $1,000, especially if you're going for professional-grade studio earphones. And if you care about active noise cancellation, you can easily spend $300 — that's the price of peace and quiet. You can also get hyperspecialized models like sleep earbuds, bone-conduction earbuds for working out, and open earbuds for transparency. The best tech deal this week The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

Recent findings suggest that in 2026, our top picks for earbuds are the Sony WF-1000XM6, Bose QuietComfort Ultra (2nd gen), and Panasonic Technics AZ100s, which provide outstanding sound quality and ANC. But keep in mind that these models will run you $299 to $329. While we stand by the value of everything on this list, we know that spending over $300 on a pair of earbuds is a lot to stomach. That's why we've also included more budget-friendly wireless earbuds under $100 that still deliver excellent performance.

Ready to start shopping now? Here are our favorite wireless and noise-cancelling earbuds as of November 2026.

Read our full review of the Sony WF-1000XM6 earbuds.

Industry observers note that anyone looking for the all-around best experience: Sony's new XM6 earbuds are the follow-up we've been waiting for from the brand. Though they cost a lot, they justify their price point in an excellent performance on all fronts, which brings some of the best ANC, sound quality, design, and ease of use to one elegant package.

Sony built a reputation for providing some of the best sound quality available in the game, and while we still think the Technics on this list eke out a better performance, Sony's overall package is unrivaled.

According to recent reports, the earbuds sound great out of the box, but the 10-band equalizer gives the user plenty of options for customization. Whether we listened to classic rock or straight-up classical concertos, these earbuds made music sound immersive, rich, and clear. To supplement the great sound quality, Sony also stepped up its ANC game from the previous gen, resulting in the best ANC we've ever encountered on a pair of earbuds. Though we wish it were adjustable (especially at this price point), if you're looking to block out the world around you as much as possible, we think these perform even better than our former favorites, the Bose QC Ultra 2 buds.

Recent findings suggest that where Bose has Sony beat is in comfort. Sony did redesign the shape of its earbuds from the previous gen, helping provide an even more comfortable and flush fit. Still, Bose's stability band still takes the cake for the best fit we've ever experienced — but Sony is closing that comfort gap.

Read our full review of the Panasonic Technics EAH-AZ100 earbuds.

Industry observers note that audiophiles first and foremost: If you want to hear every note in perfect crisp detailed sound, the Panasonic's Technics EAH-AZ100 make music better thanks to their magnetic fluid drivers. Whether you want a fully customizable experience by adjusting your bass and treble, or you just want to pop in your buds and experience delicious spatial audio without the fuss, the Technics offer owners both.

Panasonic blew us away with its Technics EAH-AZ100 earbuds. If you've ever thought that earbuds can't deliver the same potent sound quality as over-ear headphones, then let the AZ100s prove you wrong. The buds come with four different ear tips that range from extra small to large, delivering a snug and secure fit suitable for even those with small or narrow ears who struggle to find earbuds that fit. That being noted, they aren't the most comfortable headphones we've ever tested (nothing beats the Bose QuietComfort Ultras), as they get uncomfortable after a couple of hours of wear.

According to recent reports, however, what you're really after here is the incredible sound quality of the Technics. Music just sounds better on the AZ100 earbuds. The earbuds deliver music as close to the source as possible. While listening to James Brown's "The Boss," the song sounded rich and textured, with layers of horn and deep bass bursting through. Plus, it picks up on the most subtle details, like in "Angel Of My Dreams" by Jade, the soft shuttering of cameras flashing on the backing track rang through in crisp detail.

Plus, these headphones have impressive active noise cancellation. While testing them on a trip to Newly introduced York, they blocked out the clatter of the subway and ruckus of noisy streets. With such excellent ANC, nothing distracts from the superior audio quality. The three-way multipoint connection is another huge advantage of these headphones. I could seamlessly switch between my iPhone, iPad, and MacBook Pro without having to open the app.

Not to mention, these earbuds have killer battery life. They last for 10 hours with an additional 28 hours available with the charging case.

Read our full review of the Bose QuietComfort Ultra earbuds (2nd gen).

Long-haul travelers, students, or anyone who can't get earbuds to fit quite right: For those who value noise cancellation and all-day wear above all else, the $299 Bose QuietComfort Ultra earbuds (2nd gen) are worth the investment. With spatial audio and some of the best ANC we've encountered, these earbuds deliver immersive sound that envelopes you in your music.

Over-ear headphones are the typical pick for those who want the best noise cancellation, but these days, you're no longer limited if you prefer earbuds but still want top-tier ANC.

Bose's second iteration of its QuietComfort Ultra earbuds doesn't change too much from the original, with the main improvements coming in the form of wireless charging, improved speech clarity on calls, and better adaptive ANC, but we also noticed some minor improvements to the sound profile, which also did a great job of sounding full and resonant right out of the box.

Where these earbuds really shine, however, is in their name: it's their fit and noise cancellation. Though they only have three sizes of ear tips and stability bands, the design of these earbuds allows for a fit that's both secure and comfortable enough to wear for hours on end, which isn't a given with earbuds. The noise cancellation impresses, too, even without any music playing, thanks to the eight microphones packed into these buds. Common household sounds like air conditioning, neighbors, and other people existing in your space all but disappear with the ANC bumped all the way up. If you don't like that much blockage, you can turn on transparency mode or manually adjust the level of ANC.

Industry observers note that so what are the downsides? Besides being priced like a premium pair of earbuds (which, to be fair, they are in their performance), the six-hour battery life is starting to lag behind competitors. Plus, the equalizer is less sophisticated than what you'll find on other earbuds, and the touch controls weren't quite as seamless as we want on $300 earbuds. Still, for the combo of noise-cancelling and comfort, we can't choose a better pair of earbuds.

Read our full review of the Apple AirPods Pro 3.

Apple fans: Apple device owners will appreciate how easily these earbuds pair with multiple devices, as well as their impressive active noise cancellation and the many ways they can be used.

The AirPods Pro pop up on most best of lists, and though we've always been fans, the third generation takes these earbuds to a fresh level.

At the most basic level, these earbuds perform well in all the ways you'd want them to: the sound profile is robust and clear, the noise cancellation truly silences the world around you, and they pair easily to Apple devices. With this generation, Apple bumped up these buds' battery life to eight hours per charge, putting them firmly on the higher end of what's available on the market.

Industry observers note that then, there are the extra features. Apple included a built-in heart rate monitor, which can be used when you track your workouts with the Fitness app. How did it perform? "Perfectly," according to Mashable contributor Adam Doud's review. "I checked the heart rate against another device...and in every instance, the heart rate from the AirPods Pro 3 was within a beat or two per minute of the other device, so that speaks very well for its accuracy." Along with the IP57 water- and sweat-resistance and five sizes of ear tips for finding just the right fit, the AirPods Pro have become a much better pair of earbuds for working out this generation.

Finally, the live translation. At the time of writing, it's available in English, French, German, Spanish, Portuguese, and English from the UK. Doud wrote that it worked fairly accurately (as compared to movie subtitles) with a one to two second delay, making the feature viable for real-time use.

At $249, the Apple AirPods Pro 3 are on par (and even cheaper) than other premium competitors. So what's the catch? Well, for anyone looking to fine-tune their own audio experience, there's no companion app or custom equalizer, but for everything else you get, the trade-off may well be worth it.

Read our full review of the AirPods 5 with wireless charging case.

Apple fans on a budget: The AirPods Pro 3 are great, but with the addition of better noise cancellation, a wireless charging case, volume controls on the stem, and live translation to the AirPods 5 model, you can get a very similar experience for $100 cheaper, making this the best value option for Apple-centric people.

These are also a great pick for anyone who wants earbuds that sit in between an in-ear and open earbud, as they don't have an ear tip that's situated in the ear canal, but rather rest near it as a traditional earbud would.

Apple pulled a rare move by lowering the prices on the AirPods 5 while adding more features, which made our job pretty easy in recommending them. They come with 50 percent better ANC than the AirPods 4, while being $149 compared to the 4's $179. Despite being a semi-in-ear model, they provide a surprising amount of sound control. Mashable Senior Editor Stan Schroeder wrote in his review that though they struggled on higher-pitched sounds, "on an actual plane, I realized they did a pretty good job of reducing both the engines' drone and the passengers' chatter.".

Recent findings suggest that he was also particularly impressed by how they sounded for live performances, as open earbuds tend to let the wider soundstage shine more than traditional in-ear buds, which might emphasize clarity and bass — he appreciated the width of the sound. These earbuds also come with the Live Translation feature found on the AirPods Pro 3, which allows for language translation in real time, as well as a volume sliding control on the stem. You'll miss out on the more expensive earbuds' built-in heart rate monitor and Hearing Protection feature, but if neither is too crucial to you, you'd likely be better off saving the cash. The biggest difference besides the wear is perhaps the battery life: where the AirPods Pro 3 get eight hours per charge, you'll have to settle for five hours per charge with the AirPods 5, but you will have a smaller carrying case than the Pros.

According to recent reports, bargain hunters: Finding a solid pair of budget earbuds is all about balance, and the EarFun Air Pro 4 exemplify that perfectly. While not the absolute cheapest pair of earbuds you could buy, they're still less than $100 and perform at the level of earbuds double their price. For anyone looking for the best value noise-cancelling earbuds, these are our top pick.

Recent findings suggest that the EarFun earbuds don't fall into the pitfalls of other budget buds on the market. Yeah, you'll pay more than $50 pair (but only slightly if you grab them during one of their frequent sales). What you'll get in return is affordable earbuds that can adeptly handle a multipoint connection, feature a well-rounded sound profile with variation thanks to the in-app equalizer, and a battery life that can likely power you through most, if not all, of your workday.

The efficacy of the active noise cancellation is an especially standout feature of these earbuds, thanks to the absence noise breakthrough or strong hissing to supplement the power of the ANC. (Usually, one or both can be found on cheaper earbuds.) EarFun could've stopped there, but these earbuds also offer manually adjustable ANC, which isn't even a given on premium noise-cancelling earbuds. While not every level of adjustment is worth writing home about, it's still a nice addition.

Five sizes of ear tips ranging from XS to XL help with a comfortable fit and providing the best passive noise cancellation possible. Overall, these earbuds start to verge on too good to be true for their price point. The one major flaw we could find is that their on-ear touch controls verged on being both under-and overly sensitive, causing our tester to prefer toggling them off entirely in the companion app. Still, if there was one feature EarFun was going to flop on, this is maybe the least annoying of the bunch.

Read our full review of the Soundcore Sleep A30 Special earbuds.

According to recent reports, restless sleepers in noisy nighttime environments: Within a few months, Soundcore turned around and upgraded its already excellent Sleep A30 earbuds, bringing the Sleep A30 Special earbuds to the scene. For anyone who needs noise cancellation to help them get to sleep, the Sleep A30 Specials are basically your only option — thankfully, they're also one of the best valued options.

The major names in the sleep earbuds space are Ozlo and Soundcore. While Ozlo is known for being made by former Bose engineers, the $349 earbuds come at a huge price point — especially considering their lack of features in comparison to Soundcore's offerings.

According to recent reports, most notably, the Soundcore Sleep A30 Special earbuds offer active noise cancellation, the only sleep earbuds to do that other than their predecessor, the Sleep A30 earbuds. Even better, they do it at a significantly lower price point than the Ozlo buds at $229.99. While it's still a decent price to pay for earbuds solely designed for sleep, relatively speaking, A30 Specials offer some of the best value by far due to the feature set.

In addition to the ANC, the companion app offers several white noise options, including customizable soundscapes and Calm app meditations. If you prefer to stream your own audio, Soundcore's Bluetooth streaming with ANC on can last through an entire night of sleep (an upgrade from the regular A30 earbuds). The brand also recently added an patch to the app that allows customers to toggle on a timed turn-off for their audio, instead of the sleep detection option that existed at the earbuds' release.

These earbuds' case also monitors the environment in real time to provide adaptive snore masking, should the user toggle that option on. Standard features that exist on other earbuds will also be found on these buds, including a built-in alarm, sleep tracking data, and touch controls.

Read our full review of the Beats Powerbeats Pro 2 earbuds.

Runners, gym rats, and fitness fans: If you don't want to be bothered by loose or ill-fitting headphones while lifting or on a run, go for a pair that won't budge. The Beats Powerbeats Pro 2 fit snuggly within the ear, but the extra ear hook adds an extra level of security. For iOS users, these connect instantly, but even Android users can benefit from a quick Bluetooth connection, too.

Industry observers note that when you're on the go and want to stay hands-free, the Powerbeats Pro 2 have external controls for answering calls or playing music. Plus, the Powerbeats bring crisp sound that helps you block out sound when you'd rather focus on your workout and not the gym crowd around you. Not to mention, the Powerbeats also include a heart rate monitor for real-time readings.

Sources indicate that the Powerbeats Pro have earned a permanent spot in my gym bag. They fit snuggly within the ear and with the ear hooks don't budge, no matter how sweaty I get or how I move through my workouts. As an iPhone user, they're a dream to connect, automatically doing so whenever I take them out of the case.

With their noise-cancelling capabilities, they're able to block out the noise of the gym or the outdoors. But if you want to be able to hear the world around you for safety, you can swap into Transparency Mode. The sound is clear and consistent. Is it the best sound quality I've tested? No, but it's still pretty great.

The on-ear earbud controls are great. The Beats Fit Pro suffered from overly sensitive controls, causing me to accidentally end a call or two. But the controls on the Powerbeats Pro 2 don't get set off by accidentally brushing them. The battery life on the Powerbeats Pro 2 is incredible, up to 45 hours with the case. I think I went a full month without charging them — even with daily use.

Recent findings suggest that it actually wasn't love at first wear with the Powerbeats. At first, they're pretty awkward figuring out how to fit the bud in your ear and then hooking them around. Both my colleague, Bethany Allard, and I tested the Powerbeats and struggled with the learning curve of getting them to fit, and it was a bad first impression of the Beats. While I do like how customizable they are with five different ear tips, navigating their fit is difficult at first.

According to recent reports, however, after a few months of use, I realized the Powerbeats Pro 2 became my go-to gym earbud. While other earbuds didn't sound as good, started to slip out when things got sweaty, or required frequent charging, I always returned to the Powerbeats Pro 2.

Read our full review of the Bose QuietComfort earbuds.

Anyone who wants budget-friendly from a premium brand: If you want good-quality sound but don’t want to spend over $200, the Bose QuietComfort is an affordable answer to the brand’s lineup. They’re focused on a great fit, as they not only come with multiple ear tips but multiple bands that can be changed out on the earbuds for a better fit on the crest of your ear.

It has been revealed that the accompanying app lets you adjust audio levels, but you won’t need to, as these earbuds make all your music sound better. They’re reliable, have a long battery life, and are sure to please the pickiest of audiophiles.

I’ve sung the praises of the QuietComfort Ultra, but Bose’s latest earbuds, the entry-level QuietComfort, are also fantastic, especially with their under-$200 price tag. Even after adjusting the ear tips and bands, I didn’t find the fit on these quite as secure as the Ultras. However, my colleague Bethany Allard, who also tested the QuietComfort earbuds, noted they were the best earbuds that have ever fit her.

The QuietComfort’s sound quality is just phenomenal. With these earbuds, listening to Ethel Cain’s A House in Nebraska immersed me in the orchestrations. When Brick House by The Commodores came on, the earbuds elevated the snappy drum beats so that I may have been listening live.

The noise cancellation on the QuietComfort earbuds isn’t as sophisticated as the Ultras; I found they had more sound leakage and that classic ANC buzz when I was in noisy environments. However, the ANC on these is still great, especially in quiet spaces.

One tiny beef I have with the Bose QuietComfort earbuds is that they require a different app than the standard Bose one. This is annoying if you’re an existing Bose user and need to download another app; plus, this earbud app just isn’t as good as Bose’s flagship app.

All in all, these are a solid pair of headphones that, for $179, are an unbeatable value.

Read our full review of the Bose Ultra Open (2nd gen).

Anyone who finds earbuds too uncomfortable: If you want a pair of everyday earbuds with an open design, the latest Bose Ultra Open earbuds will be your best bet. Yes, $300 is a hefty investment, but they have the best sound quality of any open earbuds we've tried. Plus, Bose's clip-on design can't be beat, from the comfort to the colorways.

According to recent reports, the open earbuds trend has taken off in the past few years for anyone who craves some more awareness when listening to their audio. Maybe it's because you don't want to totally feel siloed in your own world; maybe it's convenient for exercise, more comfortable, or simply safer with their heightened awareness. Whatever your reason for wearing them, in our testing, we found the second-generation Bose Ultra Open earbuds are the best choice for most folks.

Recent findings suggest that we were already fans of the sound quality of the first-generation Bose open buds, but the second generation adds more bass and depth, making it the superior open earbud listening experience. Bose also nails the design. The clip is secure, easy to adjust, and comfortable enough to wear for hours. You'd think at least one of those areas would suffer, but Bose strikes the balance. Rounding out the top-tier design are the excellent color selection (black, white smoke, limited-edition cherry chocolate, olive green, and sky pink) and the best tactile controls you'll find on any pair of earbuds, thanks to the button on the top of the clip mechanism's back side. These buds also come with an IPX4 water and sweat resistance rating, so you're cleared for workouts.

Industry observers note that so what's the catch? Well, they're expensive as hell, even for regular noise-cancelling earbuds. If these lean too pricey, our former top pick, the Shokz OpenDots One, is still a worthwhile (and more affordable) choice for clip-on earbuds.

Read our full review of the Soundcore AeroFit 2 Pro.

According to recent reports, versatility is key: The Soundcore AeroFit 2 Pro are the jack of all (earbud) trades, master of none. They're the only real option if you want to keep open and noise cancelling earbuds with you on the go without carrying around, or paying or, two completely separate pairs of earbuds. They're not the best in either department, but they're pretty solid in both, making them an excellent option for those who value convenience above all else.

Admittedly, the pool of options is pretty much limited to the AeroFit 2 Pro when considering dual-form earbuds — unless you count the noise-reduction features on Shokz OpenFit Pro. For true noise cancellation and open form wear however, you'll have to look to the Soundcore buds.

That criteria on its own doesn't earn these earbuds a spot on our list, though. Soundcore followed through on their innovative design by producing earbuds that actually perform well, too, even with their flaws. Let's start with the weakest point: these earbuds don't come with interchangeable ear tips (á la the AirPods 4), instead staying in place with an adjustable ear hook that looks them into the noise cancelling or open mode. While still relatively comfortable, it does mean that they suffer somewhat on the passive noise cancellation front. Paired with just-okay ANC, you won't be getting the best noise blocking out there — expect to be able to somewhat make out conversations of coworkers or fellow cafe-goers, though both will be dampened.

Sources indicate that still, if the best ANC isn't a top priority, this a fairly easy feature to overlook. Especially when a quick adjustment of the ear hook, you suddenly have the best transparency mode possible — an open-ear design. Soundcore has plenty of experience making solid open earbuds, so it came as no surprise that the sound on these was clear, relatively robust, and noticeably varied, especially with equalizer adjustments. The ear hook kept them sturdy and in place, making these IP55 dust and water-resistance rated buds an excellent option for wear while working out or simply staying aware while out and about.

Sources indicate that there are two overarching types of earbuds: wireless and wired. While those descriptors are self-explanatory, let's get into the specifics of both.

Wireless earbuds connect to devices via Bluetooth for cordless usage. These earbuds range from $20 budget models to high-end models with active noise cancellation. While they don't require a wire to connect to a device, some wireless earbuds still have a wire that might go around the back of the neck to connect the buds.

Industry observers note that while earbuds traditionally don't provide the passive noise cancellation of over-the-ear headphones, wireless models often feature ANC, which electronically blocks out background noise. With wireless headphones, you need to consider the battery life. Most models should have an eight-hour or more battery life before they need to be recharged.

Wired earbuds are the original model: two buds connected by a wire to your audio source. While they once felt high-tech, they're pretty basic now. Wired earbuds with active noise cancellation are basically non-existent, other than Bose's newest release.

Sources indicate that the biggest positive of wired headphones is that they don't need to be charged. They're a great backup option to keep in your bag in case your usual wireless headphones or earbuds run out of charge.

We added the new Apple AirPods 5 with Wireless Charging Case to this guide in October following their September 2026 release as a cheaper alternative for Apple users, or for folks who don't prefer the ear tip fit of the AirPods Pro 3.

According to recent reports, after extensive testing, Mashable Lead Shopping Reporter Bethany Allard rounded up the best sleep earbuds. You can read her full guide, but as of February 2026, we've added the Anker Soundcore Sleep A30 Special to this guide, which Allard notes are the best sleep earbuds for most people. Also in February 2026, we added the Sony WF-1000XM6 earbuds as our top pick for the best overall earbud, and removed the previous generation, the WF-1000XM5, as the best Sony earbud.

It has been revealed that bose recently declared two new open earbuds: the Ultra Open (2nd gen) and Sport Open. We'll be testing them out to see how they compare to the Shokz earbuds in this guide. Bose also released a new pair of wired noise-cancelling earbuds, which are a breakthrough in the wired earbuds market.

With the announcement that Bose is acquiring Skullcandy and the release of the Noise Master Buds Open earbuds with Sound by Bose, we'll be testing more Bose-powered audio products not directly from the brand.

In a recent development, if you're just looking for a pair of everyday wireless earbuds, all but one of the models in this guide will check that box. (We formerly included the Marshall Mode earbuds for folks who preferred a wired option, but have since removed them from our guide as the version we tested is difficult to find in stock these days.).

If you're looking for the highest quality wireless earbuds, you can't go wrong with the Sony WF-1000XM6, Bose QuietComfort Ultra, Apple AirPods Pro 3, and Panasonic Technics EAH-AZ100 earbuds, our most recent recommendations in 2026. All of these wireless earbuds feature elite noise cancellation, stellar sound, long battery life, and a comfortable fit for extended wear.

Though most earbuds are now wireless, this ultimately comes down to preference. If you have a tighter budget or don't want to worry about the battery running low all the time, wired earbuds are a great option. With that noted, it is significantly harder to find wired earbuds with active noise cancellation. At the time of writing, the only pair with both wired connectivity and ANC both is from Bose — we're still in the process of testing them out.

It has been revealed that to help you decide, we put a range of wireless earbuds to the test to determine which are worth your money. Whether you're simply looking for earbuds to get you through the work day, a pair to take with you on a flight, or a pair that you can live in 24/7, we have a set of buds for you. And if nothing on this list stands out to you, you can always expand your search to headphones as well.

Sources indicate that as long as they're Bluetooth-compatible, these earbuds should connect to any smartphone, tablet, or laptop regardless of operating system. All of the earbuds on this list work equally well across iOS and Android systems with one exception — Apple AirPods.

Sources indicate that our favorite AirPods, the Apple AirPods Pro 3 are great and will connect to an Android device, but you won't get the same ease of connectivity or full array of features. However, other earbuds like the Bose QuietComfort Ultra earbuds and the Panasonic Technics AZ100 feature Android apps so you can experience their full range of features on an Android device.

Each pair of earbuds selected for this guide was hands-on tested by a Mashable reporter, editor, or contributor. Along with wireless earbuds tested specifically for this article, we also combed through our existing reviews to pick the best of the best earbuds for 2026. In addition to the bang for your buck, when testing earbuds, we consider criteria such as:.

Industry observers note that for each of our earbuds, we do our best to run their battery life out and test it against the stated battery life. All ANC earbuds are used with ANC, and while each tester defers to their preferred volume, we do try to average around the 50% mark when in use.

We tested out these earbuds with a variety of songs, from live performances to bass-heavy electronic music, R&B, rock, and folksy guitar songs. We evaluated how they sounded out of the box, along with any EQ presets or custom controls. Realistically, you'll make calls when using your earbuds, which is why we put each of these earbuds through a call test, making sure the person on the other end of the phone could hear us clearly and consistently.

According to recent reports, though this category can be subjective, we made sure each of our selections at least had several different ear tip sizes and were comfortable to wear for stretches of three hours or more. We also evaluate features like cleverly placed touch controls and stabilizers for keeping earbuds in place, both during casual use and exercise.

Sources indicate that any feature that made the earbuds stand out and also performed consistently well earned points in this category. For example, in addition to a rich out-of-the box sound profile, the Sony earbuds had an incredibly customizable and user-friendly experience with the in-app equalizer.

Bethany Allard is a Los Angeles-based shopping reporter at Mashable covering beauty tech, dating, sex and relationships, and headphones. That basically means she puts her hair through a lot, scrolls through a lot of dating apps, and rotates through a lot of different headphones. In addition to testing out and rounding up the best products, she also covers deals for Mashable, paying an especially obsessive amount of attention to Apple deals and prices. That knowledge comes in handy when she's covering shopping holidays like Prime Day and Black Friday, which she's now done for five years at Mashable.

According to recent reports, samantha Mangino, is an e-reader expert. She's tested all the Kindle and Kobo e-readers, diving into the buzziest models. Her love of reading extends beyond the e-reader beat, covering books and authors, too. In the tech space, she covers tablets, smart rings, and headphones.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, female mosquitoes use several sensory systems to locate a host whose blood they can feed on. One of these systems is a group of proteins known as ionotropic receptors, which detect the acidic compounds in human sweat that contribute to its sour smell. Writing in Nature, Xu et al.1 report 3D structures of an ionotropic-receptor complex from the malaria-spreading mosquito Anopheles stephensi. The structures show how the binding of an acid activates the receptor, which then opens its ion-conducting pore and generates an electrical signal that helps to guide the mosquito towards a human host.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The influencer who documented her battle with stage four breast cancer announced that she had died in a pre-recorded video shared to her Instagram Nov.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Christie Miller wanted her last message on this Earth to be joyful.

The influencer who documented her battle with stage four breast cancer announced that she had died in a pre-recorded video shared to her Instagram Nov. 23. She was 60.

In a recent development, “If you are seeing this video it means that I am dead,” Miller said, going on to show a supercut of images of her and late husband Mark Miller, who died in 2025 after a battle with pancreatic cancer. “That’s right. I have crossed the veil. I am sitting with my sweetie.”.

Although it was a heartbreaking parting from the content creator, she emphasized she was feeling “absolute bliss” and “no regret” in how she lived her life.

“If you are missing me, please be sad,” she continued. “It’s normal to be sad but also be happy that we got to spend time together whether it was in person friends or a chance meeting or we’ve known each other forever. What I know for sure is, life is great. Life is whatever we make it.”.

Miller—who was diagnosed with cancer in 2022—highlighted that she felt total enlightenment at the end of her life, saying she was “living at the top” of David Hawkins’ Map of Consciousness.

Sources indicate that “What’s at the top? Love, peace, gratitude, joy,” she mused. “I do not let myself slip from those places. Yes, you can be in joy and still have grief. You can be at peace knowing you’re dying. It’s all good and it’s about choosing what emotion we want to have in the time. I have lived this beautiful life with no regrets.”.

The self-proclaimed Chief Joy Officer—who donned a colorful piñata costume in the video—assured her followers that she was only feeling happy to reunite with her late husband and ended her video with some parting words of wisdom.

“My last bit of advice for you is go out there and live your life,” she shared. “Feel the fear and do it anyway. Stop freaking caring about what anyone thinks. They’re too self-involved in their own life. They’re not worried about you.”.

As she put it, “Go out there and find joy every single day.”.

For more influencers who left the world with their own parting message, keep reading….

Three years after she was diagnosed with ALS, the influencer announced her own death on social media at the age of 39.

Recent findings suggest that “I am not in pain, or tired. I can laugh, talk, and I can move,” Sara wrote in the caption of her January 2026 Instagram. “Reflecting in my last few months of my life, I am glad I didn’t go suddenly even WITH the suffering. I finished my list.”.

Referencing what she often referred to online as “the after,” she added, “Even if you don’t believe in any thing, I am feeding the earth, and my tree. I loved this life, and am grateful for the time.”.

Two months before her death, she reflected on her life and encouraged others to embrace the time they have.

“I am so thankful, and I never should have had the opportunity to make an account about my journey as a dying mom,” Sara wrote in a November 2025 blog on Her ALS Story. “Be good to each other and love the s--t out of your life.".

The former Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders choreographer who starred in Netflix’s 2020 reality show Country Ever After with ex Coffey Anderson, announced her own death at 45 following a seven-year battle with colon cancer.

“Ethan, you made me a mom. I’m still beside you, cheering you on,” she continued. “Savannah, my bonus girl—you were a gift God knew I needed. Emmarie, my Jesus-loving dancer—keep dancing through every season. Everleigh, my bright spark—chase your dreams boldly and without fear.”.

Criscilla added, “My babies… I am watching over you. When a moment feels warm, familiar, or too beautiful to be coincidence—that’s me. I’m still mothering you. I’m still yours.”.

After a five-year battle with colon cancer, influencer Tanner Martin—who documented his terminal disease and life with wife Shay Martin and daughter AmyLou online—personally announced his own death.

According to recent reports, “Hey, it’s me, Tanner,” Tanner said in a posthumous video shared to Instagram in June 2025. “If you’re watching this right now, I’m dead.”.

“Everyone, I had a heck of a life,” he continued in his video. “You guys seriously thank you for all that you do for me for the time I was here and all the support and love you showed me and my little family. I would ask at this time if you could continue to offer prayers and stuff for my sweetheart Shay and my baby girl Jiaozi.”.

The influencer expressed gratitude for his audience, noting that his final request was simply to remember his family in thoughts and prayers.

In a recent development, “Life was awesome,” Tanner concluded. “I really enjoyed it while I was here. Hopefully I believe there’s something after this and hopefully we’re hanging out now. There’s just a lot of people in the afterlife that I’m excited to see them not in pain and just happy.”.

It has been revealed that in October 2024, TikToker Bella Bradford shared that she had died after a battle with a rare form of cancer in her jaw muscle. She was 24.

It has been revealed that “I have terminal cancer and unfortunately, by now, my life has come to an end, and I’ve passed away,” Bella said in her video. “But I wanted to do one final ‘Get Ready With Me’ because I love doing these, and I love fashion. And despite the heartbreaking circumstances, Bella left followers with a hopeful note.

The Australian TV host announced her own death in an Instagram post shared in October 2024 after a three-year battle with motor neuron disease—a neurodegenerative condition similar to ALS.

And the 67-year-old did not hide the debilitating effect her disease had on the end of her life.

“Last night brought an end to a very tough few months,” she admitted. “While I’ve never wanted to die, the thought of leaving my tortured body was a relief.”.

She concluded, "So let’s not call it goodbye as I hope to see you again on the other side—I carry your love and laughter with me and hope you’ll remember mine.”.

Canadian influencer Kimberley Nix unveiled her death in May 2024 after documenting her battle with metastatic sarcoma online for three years.

Sources indicate that “Hello followers,” Kimberley said in a TikTok video. “If you’re seeing this message, I have passed away peacefully.”.

The 31-year-old influencer—who was a resident trained in internal medicine—explained that she had a “beautiful life” and shared a list of her favorite things, including her pets, her makeup collection and her husband Michael MacIsaac.

And Kimberley—who used her platform to educate followers on her condition after her 2021 diagnosis—also expressed gratitude for her online community.

“I love you all, thank you so much for this amazing opportunity,” she remarked. “I’m in happy tears because you’ve all made me find so much purpose in the end of my life.”.

Daniella Thackray, who detailed her battle with cholangiocarcinoma—a rare and aggressive form of cancer that grows in the bile ducts of one’s liver—wrote a personal note on Facebook to announce her own death in February 2024.

“If you’re reading this then it means I have died from my battle with cancer and my family are posting my final message on my behalf,” Danielle, who hailed from Leeds, United Kingdom, wrote at the time. “Although we can’t control what happens to us, we can control how we react. I chose not to mourn the life I was losing despite being so devastated, but to instead enjoy every moment I had left.”.

The 24-year-old admitted that she hoped more research would be done surrounding her cancer—which has no obvious causes or cure at this time—but emphasized that she lived her short life to the fullest.

“As I have always stated and believed you should enjoy the little things in life and cherish every moment!” Daniella wrote in her farewell. “Romanticise your life! Do whatever makes you happy and don’t let anyone take the joy of life away from you x.”.

And her final word was to her fiancé Tom Calvert, to whom Daniella wrote, “I love you and always will. Go enjoy your life now, you deserve it.”.

“Hi everyone,” Paul remarked in the video, which he said he recorded in December 2023. “If you’re watching me, I’m dead.”.

Paul noted in his video that while he thought he had caught his cancer early, it began to spread rapidly to his bones, and it became apparent to him that his time “is drawing very short.”.

As he put it, “I can’t even begin to articulate how beneficial and appreciated those things are.”.

Senegal reinstated as Afcon 2025 winners by court ruling

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1676 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sadio Mane's Senegal have been confirmed as Afcon 2025 winners following their appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport, giving the Teranga Lions a second continental title.
  • Senegal have been reinstated as winners of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations after a ruling by the Court of Arbitration for Sport.
  • The court's award overturns a previous decision which had stripped the West Africans of the title they won on the pitch during a chaotic final against host nation Morocco in January.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sadio Mane's Senegal have been confirmed as Afcon 2025 winners following their appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport, giving the Teranga Lions a second continental title.

Senegal have been reinstated as winners of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations after a ruling by the Court of Arbitration for Sport.

The court's award overturns a previous decision which had stripped the West Africans of the title they won on the pitch during a chaotic final against host nation Morocco in January.

It has been revealed that with the game goalless, Senegal left the field of play in second-half stoppage time in protest at a penalty awarded against them. The match in Rabat was delayed by over 15 minutes before Morocco's Brahim Diaz had his spot-kick saved.

Senegal then triumphed 1-0 after extra time, with Pape Gueye scoring the winner.

That result was overturned almost two months later when a Confederation of African Football (Caf) appeals board decreed the Teranga Lions had breached competition regulations by leaving the field of play after the penalty was awarded.

Senegal's football federation (FSF) subsequently appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas), sport's highest legal authority, with a three-man panel hearing its case behind closed doors in Lausanne on 8 October.

In a recent development, in a unanimous verdict, the Cas panel has effectively backed the decision by referee Jean-Jacques Ndala to restart the game after Senegal returned to the field and the match was played to a conclusion. The result of the final stands and Senegal are now confirmed as Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) 2025 winners.

A statement issued by Cas stated the court considered that "the referee's decision to resume the match or to stop it fell definitively within his sole authority".

"By blowing his whistle to restart play, the referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met - both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume.".

The FSF immediately reacted with a social media post featuring a picture of the side lifting the trophy in January captioned with the phrase "again and always champions of Africa".

"The FSF welcomes this ruling with deep satisfaction," it later stated in a statement.

"This decision affirms, above all, the triumph of sporting fairness and reaffirms a fundamental principle: the true outcome of a match is determined exclusively on the field of play, under the protection of sports law.".

Meanwhile, Morocco's football federation (FRMF) expressed "surprise" at the ruling and added that it would "pursue all available legal avenues to challenge the decision".

Caf notes it respects the Cas award and "will take all the necessary measures to implement it".

The full grounds for the decision will be published by Cas in due course unless the parties request confidentiality.

'Shameful' and 'terrible look' - the chaos that marred Afcon 2025 final.

'The longest VAR check in history' - the fallout from shock Afcon decision.

Senegal's walk-off during the final in Rabat has already brought about a change in football's rules.

"The referee may sanction with a red card any player who leaves the field of play in protest at â a âreferee's decision," said Ifab, the game's lawmaking body, in April.

"This latest rule will also apply âto any team official who incites players to leave the field of play. A team that causes a match âto be abandoned will, in principle, forfeit the match.".

Morocco and Senegal have both changed coach since the Afcon 2025 final and earlier this month secured their places at the 2027 edition of the tournament with two rounds of qualification remaining.

Referee Ndala was at the centre of the controversy during the Afcon final.

A tightly contested final between the continent's top-ranked sides produced two moments of controversy in second-half stoppage time, with referee Ndala at the centre of the drama.

First the Congolese official denied Senegal a near-certain goal, blowing his whistle for a challenge by Abdoulaye Seck on Morocco right-back Achraf Hakimi moments before Ismaila Sarr nodded in.

The free-kick looked soft, but the video assistant referee (VAR) was unable to get involved because Ndala had awarded the foul before the ball crossed the line.

Three minutes later came a flashpoint in the Senegal box, when El Hadji Malick Diouf tugged Morocco playmaker Diaz back before heading a corner clear.

Diaz vehemently claimed a penalty and Ndala eventually awarded a spot-kick after being sent to consult his pitchside monitor by the VAR.

Senegal coach Pape Thiaw called his players over to the touchline, and Thiaw subsequently headed down the tunnel to the changing room in protest against the decision - accompanied by several players.

They eventually returned, but over 15 minutes had elapsed since the award of the penalty by the time Real Madrid's Diaz failed to convert, with his Panenka-style attempt easily saved by goalkeeper Edouard Mendy.

Meanwhile, there was unrest inside the Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium as a small contingent of Senegal supporters clashed with security staff.

The game went into extra time, with midfielder Gueye scoring the goal which settled the contest in Senegal's favour.

Off the pitch, another match involving disciplinary boards and lawyers would soon begin.

Brahim Diaz's penalty was saved by Edouard Mendy after Senegal's walk-off led to a delay of over 15 minutes before he was able to take the spot-kick.

Senegal celebrated their second continental title but the FRMF rapidly lodged an appeal with Caf, arguing their opponents had breached Article 82 of Afcon regulations, which covers withdrawals.

It states that if a team "refuses to play or leaves the ground before the regular end of the match without the authorisation of the referee" it shall be "considered [the loser] and shall be eliminated for good from the current competition".

A disciplinary board from the continental game's governing body rejected the FRMF's appeal days after the final as it sanctioned and fined those found guilty of unsporting conduct during the match.

Yet in March, almost two months on from the final, a Caf appeals board ruled that Senegal had forfeited the match and awarded Morocco a 3-0 victory.

The FSF described the ruling as "unfair, unprecedented and unacceptable" and swiftly lodged its case with Cas.

The director general of the Switzerland-based court stated arbitration proceedings would be conducted "as swiftly as possible", but it was over five months until all parties descended on Lausanne for a one-day hearing.

The Cas panel was led by Frenchman Gerald Simon, founder of the Sports Law Laboratory at the University of Burgundy and a Cas member for 23 years.

Both the FRMF and FSF were able to nominate an arbitrator to exercise an independent judicial function once their appointment was confirmed.

According to recent reports, the FRMF nominated Italian international law professor Luigi Fumagalli, while the FSF nominated Hamburg-based attorney and professor of âlaw at the University of Zurich Ulrich Haas. Those two men completed the Cas panel.

Over six weeks on from that hearing - and 10 months since the Afcon 2025 final - Senegal have been proclaimed champions once again.

But the debate and damage done to the reputation of African football is likely to linger for some time yet.

Senegal reinstated as Afcon 2025 winners.

In its appeal, the FSF argued that the decision of referee Ndala to resume the match in the 19th minute of added time - and to allow it to be concluded with a sporting result - could not be reviewed, pursuant to the 'field of play' doctrine.

Cas has a long-standing practice where it refrains from "reviewing decisions taken on the playing field by referees for applying the rules of the game, unless there is evidence that those rules were applied arbitrarily or in bad faith".

The FRMF argued, on the contrary, that the referee's decision did not fall under the field of play doctrine because Senegal should have faced disciplinary consequences for walking off the pitch.

The Moroccan federation went on to argue that, according to Afcon tournament rules, the referee should have brought the match to an early conclusion.

It added that Ndala "erred in law" and that his decision was "arbitrary".

However, in the view of the panel, the referee's decisions were limited to the pitch and the relevant Afcon regulations regarding withdrawals were not applicable.

"The panel acknowledged that the referee had to make a decision in an atmosphere of extreme tension," the Cas statement added.

Recent findings suggest that "However, these circumstances do not justify describing the decision as 'arbitrary'. On the contrary, the referee's judgment did not appear to have been affected by factors external to the game.".

Court of Arbitration for Sport reinstates Senegal as Afcon winners.

Despite Cas being the highest authority in sport, and its decision coming 10 months on from the final, there could yet be a further twist.

The FRMF raised a grievance with the process before the panel's judgement was announced on Tuesday.

It alleged that German attorney Haas, the arbitrator on the panel nominated by the Senegalese, held a telephone call with FSF president Abdoulaye Fall on Sunday.

Fall "categorically" denies that any such phone call ever took place.

The FRMF notes that any unauthorised communication between a member of the panel and one of the interested parties would constitute a serious breach of Cas regulations.

It has demanded that "appropriate legal consequences be applied to actions that compromise the integrity and credibility of the arbitration process".

The Moroccans could appeal against the ruling by taking the case to the Swiss Federal Tribunal, and the country's highest court could set Cas' judgement aside.

The case would then likely be heard again at Cas, with a different panel in place.

A precedent would be the case of Chinese swimmer Sun Yang, who had an appeal against the decision by Cas to impose an eight-year doping ban upheld by the Swiss Federal Tribunal.

A newly introduced panel heard his case at Cas, and his ban was reduced to four years and three months.

#82051. Rembrandt's 'The Night Watch' is more alive than you'd expect

Rembrandt's 'The Night Watch' is more alive than you'd expect

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (949 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Rembrandt van Rijn's "The Night Watch" is one of the most famous paintings of the Dutch Golden Age.
  • Recent findings suggest that in the painting, Rembrandt made dramatic use of light and shadow to guide the viewer's eye to key figures.
  • Beyond the sense of movement featured in "The Night Watch," the painting itself is also alive in a way that's rarely taken into consideration — through the microscopic organisms living on the canvas.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rembrandt van Rijn's "The Night Watch" is one of the most famous paintings of the Dutch Golden Age. Amsterdam's Rijksmuseum, where the work is on display, hails the artist's 1642 masterpiece as "the turning point in his career and as the superlative example of his creative genius.".

Recent findings suggest that in the painting, Rembrandt made dramatic use of light and shadow to guide the viewer's eye to key figures. And unlike static group portraits typical of his era, the artist depicted Amsterdam's civic guards in mid-action, as they prepare to march out.

Beyond the sense of movement featured in "The Night Watch," the painting itself is also alive in a way that's rarely taken into consideration — through the microscopic organisms living on the canvas.

The research project "The Night Watch Lives" explores exactly that question: What kinds of life forms inhabit the surface of the famous painting?

The study is a collaborative scientific and exhibition project between the Rijksmuseum and ARTIS-Micropia — an Amsterdam museum dedicated to the world of microorganisms.

It's part of the broader "Operation Night Watch" restoration and research project described as the "biggest and most wide-ranging ever study and restoration of Rembrandt's most famous painting," started in 2019. Conservators and scientists in this project have been examining every aspect of Rembrandt's masterpiece using cutting-edge technology, seeking latest insights into its materials, condition and history — and now, its microbiome.

According to recent reports, the idea behind "The Night Watch Lives" was to "put microbes in a positive spotlight," Eline van Bloois, who led the research, told DW. "Honestly, if you're asking me — I'm a microbiologist, so I'm biased of course — but they really deserve more positive attention.".

Over a period of six months, van Bloois will be taking samples once a month directly from the famous painting at the Rijksmuseum, accompanied by the people working on the restoration of "The Night Watch.".

Using small sterile discs gently pressed against selected areas of the painting, the samples collect microscopic material from both varnished and unvarnished sections.

These samples are then cultivated in laboratories, allowing previously invisible microbes to grow into visible colonies that can be studied and identified.

At the "The Night Watch Lives" exhibition, visitors can view Petri dishes containing the cultivated microbial colonies. A life-size reproduction of Rembrandt's masterpiece also reveals where the samples were taken, and which microorganisms were found there.

Sources indicate that at the exhibition's opening on November 11, the installation included the findings of two of van Bloois' sampling sessions. Four more will be added over the coming months, allowing the museum's visitors to follow the results of the study as it unfolds.

In a recent development, that means the exhibition's visitors "will be figuring out what I've found as I'm figuring it out myself," explains the microbiologist. "We really take them through that journey with us.".

People often fear microbes or associate them with disease, even though the vast majority of these microscopic organisms are actually harmless or vital to human survival.

Some of the organisms found on the painting "are very commonly found on human skin, for instance, and they're a healthy part of the microbiome; most humans actually have these bacteria with them," notes van Bloois, adding that the presence of these microbes on the painting made sense, since humans are often near the work.

In a recent development, but another bacterium stood out in the samples: Microbacterium saccharophilum, a species first identified at a sugar refinery in Japan in 2013. How this microorganism ended up on the Dutch "Night Watch," or when, is a guessing game.

In a recent development, "It's part of the fun and part of the frustration in microbiology. You cannot ask the microbes where they originate from," notes van Bloois. "It would make our lives a bit easier, but it's also fun to have a little bit of a mystery.".

According to recent reports, the samples also revealed bacteria from soil, often found in plant roots. Could these organisms somehow harm the painting? Could plants start growing on the work?

Van Bloois explains why this is highly unlikely: On the painting, the bacteria can form inactive spores, but for the study, the researcher "provided them with all the nutrients and the right temperature and the right humidity that allowed them to grow again.".

Still, studying these organisms may eventually contribute to understanding how paintings age, how environmental conditions affect cultural heritage, and how museums can better preserve priceless works of art.

As to whether the microorganisms could date back to Rembrandt's time, the microbiologist states that's also "highly unlikely" — but here again, microbes cannot reveal their origin story.

As part of the larger "Operation Night Watch" team, van Bloois is definitely inspired by this "group effort where everyone is just really enthusiastic about telling these stories and adding to the knowledge surrounding 'The Night Watch.'".

The microbiological samples revealed by the laboratory process resemble abstract art in miniature: colorful clusters, delicate textures and intricate patterns created by living organisms.

And as the study is unfolding publicly, it also feels like an artistic performance of its own.

The project also perfectly embodies the full name of the museum where the exhibition is held: Natura Artis Magistra, a Latin phrase that translates to "nature is the teacher of art and science," as the microbiologist points out: "It's really cool to see science and art all come together in this project.".

The exhibition "The Night Watch Lives" runs at ARTIS-Micropia in Amsterdam until the end of May 2027.

Ariane 6 rocket successfully launches 36 Amazon Leo satellites into orbit after delay (video)

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, amazon's first satellite launch since a rocket failure that doomed 40 of its spacecraft went off without a hitch Tuesday morning (Nov.
  • An Ariane 6 rocket carrying 36 satellites for the Amazon Leo constellation lifted off at 6:14 a.m.
  • Sources indicate that the launch was originally supposed to take place on Monday (Nov.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, amazon's first satellite launch since a rocket failure that doomed 40 of its spacecraft went off without a hitch Tuesday morning (Nov. 24).

An Ariane 6 rocket carrying 36 satellites for the Amazon Leo constellation lifted off at 6:14 a.m. EST (1114 GMT) from Europe's Spaceport in Kourou, French Guiana, on Tuesday (Nov. 23), right at the end of the 29-minute window that opened at 6:45 a.m. EST (1045 GMT; 7:45 a.m. local time in Kourou).

Sources indicate that the launch was originally supposed to take place on Monday (Nov. 23), but that attempt was scrubbed due to a technical issue affecting the rocket's ground support systems, according to Arianespace.

Amazon Leo, so named because it will operate in low Earth orbit, will compete with SpaceX's Starlink internet constellation, which right now consists of more than 11,000 operational spacecraft.

Amazon's network will eventually have more than 3,200 satellites, but just 400 or so have reached orbit to date. Another 40 were supposed to be delivered on Nov. 15, but they were lost after their rocket ride, a United Launch Alliance (ULA) Vulcan Centaur, suffered a problem shortly after launch.

Recent findings suggest that ariane 6 and Vulcan Centaur aren't the only rockets Amazon is depending on to build its broadband constellation. Jeff Bezos' company has also booked rides on ULA's Atlas V rocket, Blue Origin's New Glenn and SpaceX's Falcon 9.

Vulcan will be grounded for a while as ULA investigates the Nov. 15 failure and works to fix whatever caused it. And New Glenn hasn't flown since April, when the rocket failed to deliver AST SpaceMobile's BlueBird 7 satellite to the proper orbit. New Glenn's return to flight was further complicated on May 28, when the rocket exploded during a routine prelaunch test.

In a recent development, the Ariane 6, the successor to Arianespace's Ariane 5 heavy lifter, debuted in July 2024 and has nine launches under its belt to date. All of them have been successful except that maiden mission, which was a partial failure.

This morning's launch was the fourth Amazon Leo flight for the Ariane 6, following introduces in February, April and June of this year.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Musk addressed the change Monday afternoon, tweeting, “as promised” above an image of a year-old conversation in which another user suggested that Musk “just buy Twitter” and “change the bird logo to a doge.”.
  • Recent findings suggest that elon Musk's Twitter promised a purge of blue check marks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Twitter’s traditional bird icon was booted and replaced with an image of a Shiba Inu, an apparent nod to dogecoin, the joke cryptocurrency that CEO Elon Musk is being sued over.

Musk addressed the change Monday afternoon, tweeting, “as promised” above an image of a year-old conversation in which another user suggested that Musk “just buy Twitter” and “change the bird logo to a doge.”.

Recent findings suggest that elon Musk's Twitter promised a purge of blue check marks. Instead he singled out one account.

The doge logo appeared on the site two days after Musk asked a judge to throw out a $258 billion racketeering lawsuit accusing him of running a pyramid scheme to support the dogecoin, according to Reuters.

Lawyers for Musk and Tesla called the lawsuit by dogecoin investors a “fanciful work of fiction” over Musk’s “innocuous and often silly tweets.”.

Sources indicate that it wasn’t clear whether the logo change was permanent. Musk has been known to use Twitter to troll both his fans and his critics.

The price of dogecoin, which is typically volatile, was up more than 20% over the past 24 hours, to about 9 cents. It was trading just under 8 cents Monday morning.

Dogecoin was created December 6, 2013, by a pair of software engineers — as a joke. The name is a nod to the “doge” meme that became popular a decade ago. Its Shiba Inu mascot mimicks that meme: a dog surrounded by a bunch of Comic Sans text in broken English.

Pochettino leads Man Utd fury at Yoro red card ruling

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester United defender Leny Yoro (second left) is shown a red card by referee Sam Barrott at Anfield.
  • Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino has questioned the competence of video assistant referee officials after defender Leny Yoro had his red card overturned by the Football Association.
  • Yoro was sent off eight minutes into United's 4-0 defeat at Liverpool on Sunday after bringing down Aleksander Isak just outside the United penalty area.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United defender Leny Yoro (second left) is shown a red card by referee Sam Barrott at Anfield.

Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino has questioned the competence of video assistant referee officials after defender Leny Yoro had his red card overturned by the Football Association.

Yoro was sent off eight minutes into United's 4-0 defeat at Liverpool on Sunday after bringing down Aleksander Isak just outside the United penalty area.

United sources say they have conclusive proof it was impossible for Isak to reach the ball after he took a heavy touch, that it would have run on to goalkeeper Senne Lammens and Yoro should not have been punished for denying a goalscoring opportunity.

Pochettino mentioned he had some sympathy with referee Sam Barrott but he is livid at how the situation played out.

According to recent reports, "I am very disappointed," the Argentine stated. "This type of thing can never happen.

Sources indicate that "We can accept the referee can make a mistake. But if we have VAR, what were they doing? What were they doing? Are we going to repeat the game? Are we going to have the possibility to play 11 by 11? No.

"We have an unbelievable car, but we need to be at the level to drive [it]. We accept that the technology is there but what are they doing?".

United are furious at both the nature of the audio of the incident, and referees' chief Howard Webb defending referee Barrott's decision and the VAR John Brooks' reinforcing it on the Mic'd Up programme, which was shown on Sky Sports.

They intend to take the matter up with both the Premier League and ProRef.

It is the second time this season United been on the wrong end of a major VAR error.

'And the three points?' - Pochettino after Yoro red overturned.

Webb apologised to United after Erling Haaland's winner in the Manchester derby at Old Trafford on 13 September was allowed to stand even though a clearly offside Enzo Fernandez was interfering with play.

There has been no apology from Webb on this occasion.

Instead, he has doubled down on the call, saying: "I think, by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving promptly on towards that ball.".

United sources claim this interpretation is wrong.

The club are unhappy at the speed the on-field decision was confirmed. It is thought United used data around Isak's top speed and his chances of reaching the ball in their defence of Yoro to the FA. They claim this could have been done "within minutes" of the incident occurring.

This is not the only bone of contention at Old Trafford around the incident.

Pochettino also pointed out Liverpool forward Bradley Barcola was too close to the United wall from the resulting free-kick and Dominik Szoboszlai's opening goal should have been disallowed.

"No-one talked about [the fact] that the goal wasn't legal," said Pochettino. "Barcola was touching our wall. It must be disallowed.

Recent findings suggest that "We need to defend my players and my club, and that is to denounce it and to say, the decision wasn't good. And now, the three points, where are the three points?".

What referee's chief Webb stated about the incident on the Mic'd Up programme.

Industry observers note that "There's a question mark, I guess, around whether or not he would get onto that ball before Lammens. Now, in the moment, the referee looked at it and felt he would.

"That was the referee's call made on the field, and then the VAR checks that to see whether that decision made on the field was clearly and obviously incorrect, and formed the opinion that it wasn't.

"That if there was any doubt, then it was doubt.

In a recent development, "It wasn't going to be something that was clearly and obviously wrong and therefore allowed that decisive on-field decision to stand. and.

"I think, by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball.

"The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it's a little bit debatable. Certainly not clearly wrong.".

Why was Yoro's red card overturned?

United's fury over Yoro and the way the situation has been handled cannot completely obscure the fact they lost 4-0 in Pochettino's first game in charge.

It extended a terrible start to the season that has seen the Red Devils win on just three occasions - and only once in the Premier League, against newly-promoted Ipswich in August.

The club are 19th in the Premier League and facing up to the possibility of being relegated for the first time since 1973-74.

Yet Pochettino is adamant there is no fragility about his latest squad.

It has been revealed that "The situation is fragile in [terms of] the environment, or the people want it to look like we're fragile. But I don't say that we are fragile. I think we are strong.

"We have great mentality and a great mindset.

Recent findings suggest that "There are many things we need to improve. It's normal to be in a different position, and everyone can use different words to describe the situation.

"But we are a strong team. They showed that last season, capable of finishing third. I think we are going to turn around the situation and start to perform in the level like before Bruno [Fernandes] said, deserve to be at this club.".

Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino (left) and skipper Bruno Fernandes speak to the media ahead of the Champions League clash with Sporting in Lisbon.

Skipper Bruno Fernandes revealed at the weekend talks over a newly introduced United contract were on hold.

The 32-year-old's present deal expires in the summer, although the club have an option to extend it by 12 months.

Speaking alongside Pochettino at a media conference before his first meeting with Sporting since he left to join United in a Â£47m deal in January 2020, Fernandes remarked his sole focus at present is to drag United out of the mire.

"For us to start winning games, then we can start speaking about contract," he noted.

"It's not vital now. It's irrelevant. Obviously, I know it's my future and I probably shouldn't look into that way because I haven't got much left in my contract, but I'm not really worried about that.

"I'm more worried about getting results, trying to bring the club back in a position that we can be proud of, and we're not there at the moment.".
